papers.title: PolyRoute: A Twelve-Language and Code-Mixed Benchmark for Typed-Decision Routing, with Baselines and a Leaderboard
papers.abstract: Typed-decision encoders answer a question about a text in one forward pass, but their behaviour outside English is rarely measured on a fixed yardstick. We release PolyRoute: 322 native-language support messages in 12 languages and 9 writing systems, 156 code-mixed or romanised messages (Hinglish, Spanglish, Arabizi), 967 optional native training rows, and a protocol for a three-way department-routing decision. Labels come from Qwen3.8-27B with a blind second pass (91% of candidates kept); an independent model, gemma4-31b, agrees on 97.2% of test items, and the largest character 5-gram similarity between any test text and any training text is 0.33. A leaderboard of 13 systems gives 61.2% for the English-root checkpoint, 77.3% for the shipped multilingual one and 96.6% for the best fine-tune; TF-IDF with logistic regression reaches 91.9%. On four withheld languages the three multilingual systems score 77%, 90% and 93%. On code-mixed text the English root (85%) is nominally ahead of the shipped multilingual checkpoint (79%; p=0.134). The split resolves differences only above about 4 points. All texts and labels are LLM-generated.

authors.name: Sarun Kumar K S
authors.institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Deceleration without identification: testing a power-law trend in Bitcoin prices under persistent noise
papers.abstract: Plotted against time since its first block on logarithmic axes, the price of Bitcoin lies close to a straight line, and a power law in time has been proposed as its long-run trend. A good fit is weak evidence: when deviations from a trend are as persistent as a random walk, regressions on time find trends and high $R^2$ where none exist. We first bound what fifteen years of weekly prices can reveal, then test only what is answerable. Using a few low-frequency averages, invariant to the noise scale and calibrated over a declared family of persistent deviations with a four-year cycle and declining volatility, we test constant drift in expected log price against an added log-age term. The procedure was fixed, validated and publicly hashed before it was applied once. Constant drift is rejected under this family at nominal 5%, and a log-age coefficient of 5.7, close to the published exponent, is not rejected. The rejection does not survive allowing persistence beyond a random walk, and a Gompertz curve with a ceiling fits about as well as the power law. Whether deviations revert to the trend cannot be decided. Registered forecasts for 2027-2030 will be scored by future prices.

papers.title: Gradient Inversion through Linear and Affine Subspace Constraints
papers.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple clients to collaboratively train a machine-learning model without directly sharing their local datasets. However, as prior works have shown, the gradients exchanged during training may reveal sensitive information about client data. Most existing attacks usually optimize dummy inputs to match the true client gradients (Gradient Inversion Attacks), while some attempt to reconstruct them based on the observation that aggregate gradients from a fully connected (FC) layer are a linear combination of its inputs. In this work, we extend this observation by showing that aggregate gradients from an FC layer with the correct scaling are actually an affine combination of its inputs. We evaluate a gradient inversion attack that leverages either known linear-subspace information or its affine-subspace counterpart at each FC layer to improve reconstruction accuracy. Our results show that subspace-based methods can substantially improve reconstruction quality over the chosen baselines in certain settings. We further demonstrate that moderate overestimation of the batch size can generally improve or preserve reconstruction quality, even when the true batch size is unknown. We additionally examine reconstruction under gradient perturbations introduced by a differential privacy (DP) mechanism, providing insight into the effectiveness of the considered formulations under noisy conditions.

papers.title: On Poincar\'e-Type Inequalities for Flags of Distributions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish enumerative formulas and derive geometric inequalities for flags of holomorphic distributions on complex manifolds. First, given a codimension-one holomorphic distribution $\mathcal{G}$ on a complex manifold $M$, we establish an upper bound for the number of independent holomorphic $p$-distributions tangent to $\mathcal{G}$ with a prescribed associated twisting line bundle $\mathcal{L}$. As an application, we prove Poincar\'e-type degree inequalities for flags on certain classes of manifolds. Finally, we investigate the Mumford--Takemoto stability of the tangent sheaves of rank-two distributions. In particular, we establish several stability results for such distributions on projective spaces, smooth weighted complete intersection threefolds, and, in particular, on smooth hypersurfaces $V\subset\mathbb{P}^4$.

papers.title: Rank Reversals in Efficient Vectors for Pairwise Comparisons
papers.abstract: Studied are the orders among alternatives given by efficient vectors for a reciprocal matrix A. The focus is upon: 1) existence of efficient vectors with a given order and 2) discrepancies between the ranking for a pair of alternatives resulting from an efficient vector and from the corresponding entry of A, called rank reversals. We use matrix intervals in which the consistent matrices built from efficient vectors lie. The existence of efficient vectors (or those from constituent convex subsets) with a rank reversal at a given position is characterized. The minimum number of rank reversals for a reciprocal matrix among all weight vectors is described and it is shown that there is an efficient vector that has this number of rank reversals. A way to construct such a vector is given. The order transitive and the uniformly ordered reciprocal matrices are shown to be, respectively, the matrices for which there is an efficient vector with no rank reversals and the matrices for which all efficient vectors have no rank reversals. The effects on rank reversals of addition and deletion of alternatives are also discussed. Using numerical experiments, the frequencies of rank reversals in certain formulaic weight vectors are given.

papers.title: W-ISA: Transactional Execution of Weight-Space Intervention Programs
papers.abstract: We present W-ISA, a software instruction set and transactional runtime for executing weight-space intervention programs on pretrained language models. Shape-checked instructions express parameter updates, projections, ablations, and rank-one transformations. The runtime applies these programs within request-scoped execution contexts and restores saved parameters after completion or interruption. Activation-based match-action rules connect measured model states to intervention selection. We evaluate restoration and replay on SmolLM-135M-Instruct and Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, and compare materialized rank-one updates with equivalent PyTorch hooks on the latter. In 45 timed requests, both intervention implementations produce identical greedy sequences at 32, 128, and 512 tokens; their maximum prompt-logit difference is 0.000184. On the complete WikiText-2 raw test split, the combined SmolLM attention-head ablation and MLP projection changes perplexity from 22.2353 to 22.3188, a relative increase of 0.3754%. W-ISA separates intervention specification, execution, and measurement, making parameter-level experiments reproducible and composable.

papers.title: NCP: Verifier-Guided Optimization of Weight-Space Control Policies
papers.abstract: We present the Neural Control Plane (NCP), a closed-loop system that observes language-model execution, synthesizes candidate weight-space intervention rules, evaluates them, and maintains a versioned table of admitted policies. NCP separates a pretrained model's inference data plane from the control policy that selects temporary parameter interventions. W-ISA supplies transactional execution and parameter restoration; NCP supplies telemetry, candidate synthesis, admission criteria, priorities, and rule lifetime management. The optimization state consists of active rules and an archive of evaluated candidates, while base-model parameters are restored after each request. In a local SmolLM-135M-Instruct experiment, NCP generated three candidates from development telemetry and evaluated them on separate task examples and a 4,095-target WikiText-2 slice. One projection reduced validation token repetition from 0.4133 to 0.2191, with a perplexity change of -0.0574%. All candidates produced zero newly correct exact answers, so the configured admission gate archived all three and retained the original active policy. Fresh-process repetition and saved-table resumption reproduced the measured outcomes. NCP provides an executable framework for studying recursive self-improvement at the control-policy level through explicit synthesis, verification, and state transitions.

papers.title: Sckwoky at SHROOM-Visions: Character-Level Hallucination-Span Detection in Image-Conditioned VLMs via Dual-Prompted LoRA Decoders
papers.abstract: We present our system for the SHROOM-visions 2026 shared task on character-level hallucination span detection in image-conditioned vision-language model (VLM) responses, evaluated across English, French, Italian, and Chinese. The detector is built on a frozen Gemma-4-12B-it backbone with trainable LoRA adapters (approximately 10.7M parameters). Because the backbone is a causal decoder, hidden states read from a single copy of an answer cannot attend to subsequent tokens; we therefore repeat the candidate answer within one prompt and extract features from its second occurrence, giving every position approximate bidirectional context in a single non-autoregressive pass. A character-level locator combines intermediate hidden states to predict hallucination probabilities, BIO boundaries, and a response-level abstention score, while separate language-specific classifiers assign one of five hallucination types to each predicted span. On the closed test set, our system reaches a macro-averaged character IoU of 0.4404, more than doubling the official baseline (0.1854), and ranks 5th-6th on IoU across the four languages. On the English tuning split, controlled ablations attribute a gain to the repeated answer that is comparable to that of LoRA adaptation (its held-out gain is smaller and concentrated on hallucinated answers), and they show that the detector relies on the image-answer pairing: shuffling images across examples drives IoU down to the level of the predict-nothing floor or below it in every language. In deployments where the same Gemma-4-12B-it model also generates answers, its base weights can be reused, making the approach practical for local question-answering systems that cannot run a separate verifier.

authors.name: Ivan Bondarenko
authors.institution: Institute for Physics and Power Engineering

papers.title: Lengthscale Estimation for the Gaussian Kernel and Deterministic Response Functions
papers.abstract: The uncertainty estimates Gaussian processes output rely on the chosen covariance kernel and its hyperparameters. We study the fixed-domain asymptotics of the maximum likelihood and cross-validation estimators of the lengthscale parameter of the popular infinitely smooth Gaussian kernel when the observations are produced by a fixed univariate response function. No theoretical results for Gaussian lengthscale estimation exist in this setting. We prove lower bounds on the lengthscale estimators that depend on the regularity of the response function, as measured by the rate of decay of its Fourier transform. If the response function lives in the Hilbert space of the Gaussian kernel with lengthscale $\ell$, the lower bounds have a straightforward dependency on $\ell$. For bandlimited functions and functions whose Fourier transforms decay as $\exp(-a \lvert \omega \rvert^\gamma)$ for $a > 0$ and $\gamma > 2$, we prove that the estimators blow up essentially at least as fast as $(\log n)^{(\gamma-2)/(2\gamma)}$ in the number of data points, $n$. Bandlimited functions are identified with $\gamma = \infty$. Unlike analogous results for finitely smooth Mat\'ern kernels, our results make no assumptions on the geometry of the observation points. Numerical experiments illustrate the results.

papers.title: Bayesian inverse problems and epidemic-threshold uncertainty for a heterogeneous SIS reaction-diffusion model
papers.abstract: We study Bayesian inference of persistence from early observations of a heterogeneous susceptible--infected--susceptible (SIS) reaction--diffusion model with standard incidence. We show that the leading prevalence dynamics depend on the unknown coefficients only through the difference between the transmission and recovery rates and the infected diffusivity. The same pair determines the principal eigenvalue whose sign governs persistence, so early prevalence can inform the threshold even when the individual rates remain uncertain. We prove global weak well-posedness and quantitative parameter stability for the SIS system and use the resulting observation-map estimates to establish Bayesian well-posedness. For an initial infection of size $\varepsilon$, we derive a uniform second-order expansion that describes how the separate rates enter prevalence. Incidence depends explicitly on transmission at leading order. When the noise standard deviation is proportional to $\varepsilon$, we prove $O(\varepsilon)$ convergence in Hellinger distance of the nonlinear posteriors to their low-prevalence limits for both prevalence alone and joint prevalence and incidence data. We bound the principal eigenvalue using the growth rate of the infected $L^2$ norm between two times. This rate gives a lower bound for the full nonlinear system, and the upper bound separates spatial transients from nonlinear saturation. Uniform spectral estimates and bounds on infection size and measurement error give sufficient conditions for persistence and extinction. We also bound the error in posterior persistence probabilities under forward and eigenvalue approximation, accounting for posterior mass near the threshold. Numerical examples illustrate threshold inference and the predicted \(O(\varepsilon)\) convergence of the nonlinear posteriors to their low-prevalence limits in Hellinger distance.

papers.title: Evaluation protocols for historical script classification: the cost of manuscript-level leakage and the role of soft labels
papers.abstract: A paleographer applies a script type classifier to unseen manuscripts. We measure how much testing on other pages of training manuscripts inflates accuracy. On VML-HP-ext (715 pages, 171 Hebrew manuscripts, 14 script classes) we compare page-level and manuscript-level splits. Page-level accuracy drops from 97% to 54% (59% at manuscript level), and is 39% on the official blind test set. The gap of 40 to 47 percentage points (pp) at patch, page and manuscript level is statistically significant and reproduces with ResNet18; on binarized patches (ink and background only) it is 34 to 42 pp, also significant. On unseen manuscripts the model is overconfident: mean confidence 70% against 54% correct pages; patch-level expected calibration error (ECE, mean gap between confidence and accuracy) rises from 0.065 to 0.444. Binarization leaves patch-level overconfidence but cuts it markedly at page level. Confidence still helps triage: in the more confident half of pages 67% are correct, 41% in the rest. Training on expert soft labels showed no evidence of an accuracy difference, though a small page-level loss cannot be ruled out. The predicted distributions are closer to the expert's assessment. ECE is lower at patch level (0.21 to 0.31) and in most runs at page level, but not significantly at manuscript level. Label smoothing (blurring the label, no expert input) also lowers ECE but comes no closer to the expert. Temperature scaling (post-training confidence correction) helps significantly only at patch level. On 97 pages of 16 manuscripts with mixed expert assessment, soft labels cut divergence from the expert by 22 to 30% (significant in four of five runs); the point estimate of accuracy is 16.5 to 23.7 pp below hard labels, but with 16 manuscripts the loss can neither be confirmed nor ruled out. We propose recommendations for the evaluation protocol; code will be released with the paper

papers.title: Quadratic Bendixson criterion for delay systems: a numerical implementation
papers.abstract: We present a software implementation (as a Python package) of approximation schemes for verifying frequency inequalities arising from the quadratic Bendixson criterion for systems of delay equations (with a single delay in the linear part). In applications to dissipative nonlinear autonomous systems, such inequalities ensure global stability. The theoretical foundations of this approach were developed in our related work. In particular, it was shown that the transfer operators involved into the frequency inequalities can be represented as integral operators with bounded kernels of the Hardy--Volterra type. Here, we use this representation to construct approximation schemes based on finite-dimensional truncations of the transfer operators. Examples of using the package are provided.

authors.name: Andrey Romanov
authors.institution: Siberian Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences

papers.title: StaRSE: Compact Russian Sentence Embeddings with a Sign-Coded Static Encoder
papers.abstract: Transformer sentence encoders provide strong retrieval quality, but their inference cost becomes a bottleneck when embeddings must be produced on CPUs or refreshed frequently. We introduce StaRSE, a compact Russian static sentence encoder that removes Transformer inference at deployment time: token directions are stored as sign bits, token norms are stored separately, and sentences are encoded by mean pooling over norm-scaled sign directions. StaRSE is initialized from ruBERT-base, fine-tuned on Russian adjacent-sentence and task-shaped pairs, and post-trained with a contrastive stage that directly optimizes the sign-projected token table. On RuMTEB, StaRSE reaches a task mean of $51.16$, $7.98$ points above the strongest included static baseline. The packaged model occupies $11.3$ MiB and has a mean CPU latency of $0.08$ ms per sentence, compared with an estimated $55.7$ MiB 16-bit parameter footprint and $1.43$ ms mean CPU latency for the closest-quality contextual encoder. Ablations examine adjacent-sentence supervision, token norms, and direct sign-projected post-training.

authors.name: Egor Soldatov
authors.institution: Siberian State University Geosystems and Technology

papers.title: Agentic AI Meets Formal Verification in the Era of Agentic Hardware Development
papers.abstract: As AI agents become increasingly capable of generating and optimizing hardware circuits, ensuring the correctness of AI-generated designs becomes more important. Meanwhile, advances in AI lower the barriers to developing and applying formal methods, creating new opportunities to automate and improve hardware verification. This invited paper presents an overview of the methodologies and applications of hardware formal methods in the AI era. First, we examine how agentic AI advances hardware formal methods across three levels: specification, proof construction, and reasoning engines. Second, we discuss how formal methods support reliable AI-driven hardware development through RTL generation, debugging, and correctness-preserving optimization. We review representative research alongside our recent contributions, highlighting key technical advances and insights from experimental results. Finally, we discuss future research opportunities toward proof-native hardware development, where formal reasoning could become an integral part of autonomous hardware design.

papers.title: Toward Autonomous RTL and Synthesis Optimization: Benchmarking and Self-Improving Agents
papers.abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) and autonomous agents are creating new opportunities for hardware design optimization. This paper examines three connected directions toward autonomous RTL and synthesis optimization: (1) Realistic benchmarking. We discuss reference-based and open-ended RTL optimization benchmarks that evaluate optimization opportunities under realistic EDA workflows. (2) Tool-grounded RTL optimization. We present Dr. RTL, a multi-agent framework that automates critical-path analysis, RTL rewriting, and implementation-level evaluation, while continuously improving through reusable optimization skills. Evaluated on 20 real-world RTL designs, Dr.~RTL achieves average WNS/TNS improvements of 21\%/17\% with a 6\% area reduction over commercial synthesis. (3) Design-specific synthesis optimization. We explore agent-driven synthesis script tuning and the discovery of executable synthesis algorithms across intermediate representations, technology-independent optimization, and technology mapping. Finally, we envision AI-native design automation that jointly explores architectural, RTL, and EDA algorithm design spaces, guided by verification constraints and implementation feedback.

papers.title: A Strategic Freight Market Model for Liner Shipping: Pricing, Entry, and Endogenous Service Choice
papers.abstract: National freight transport models usually treat prices and service provision as exogenous. This paper models both as outcomes of strategic interaction among operators of scheduled, loop-based freight services. It compares oligopolistic competition, monopoly, Ramsey pricing with service-level or system-wide cost recovery, and welfare-maximising planning. Shippers across multiple segments choose between direct cyclic liner services and an outside option, using logit demand. Operators select from candidate port rotations, vessel classes and speeds, and set origin-destination prices subject to leg capacities. Under competition, each operator offers one service. Equilibrium requires that no operator can profitably enter, exit or replace its service after prices re-equilibrate. The solution method computes global pricing best responses and tests all unilateral service deviations, pruning only those excluded by an analytical profit bound. All regimes use the same demand and cost structure. In a synthetic Baltic-North Sea application, multinomial logit competition sustains more overlapping services and lower prices than monopoly. System-wide Ramsey pricing captures most of the planner's welfare gain without a deficit. Fuel-price and demand shocks affect competitive prices through changes in the service set. When maritime services are close substitutes, entrants avoid overlapping markets and competition can reproduce monopoly outcomes. The results illustrate mechanisms rather than forecast actual markets, showing how market organisation shapes service provision, prices, modal shares and welfare.

papers.title: The Multiscale Principle in phase transition: Geometric structure, thermodynamic entropy, and dynamical instability
papers.abstract: Scaling and multi-scaling are two guiding principles for understanding nature or even commerce and industrial outcome. In the realm of critical phenomena, scaling laws describe the behavior of physical quantities near a continuous phase transition. This is a complex phenomena where systems exhibit critical fluctuations and long-range correlations, challenging classical formulations such as the fluctuation-dissipation theorem (FDT). In particular, near critical points, the divergence of the correlation length and the emergence of fractal geometry in spin clusters suggest the need for alternative frameworks. In this work, we explore the connection between critical exponents, fractal dimensions, and the thermodynamic formalism known as the Principium Luxuriae. By linking the thermodynamic fractal dimension D to the correlation length and entropy variations, we reinterpret energy dissipation in terms of multiscale processes. This approach allows us to reproduce effective scaling tendencies associated with the critical behavior of the 2d Ising model and provides new insight into how systems redistribute energy macroscopically during phase transitions. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the decrease in D near the critical temperature marks a transition toward macroscopic coherence, where the system begins to dissipate energy across its entire scale. This unified behavior, however, induces a heightened sensitivity to perturbations, where local fluctuations are transmitted globally through the fractal network. This mechanism establishes a direct bridge between geometric structure, thermodynamic entropy, and the onset of dynamical instability (chaos) as the system approaches criticality.

papers.title: CAppleNet: A Coordinate Attention-Based YOLO11 for Real-Time Apple Stem Cavity and Calyx Detection
papers.abstract: Automated fruit grading, sorting, and orientation systems require real-time, accurate detection of fruit-level morphological landmarks rather than the fruit boundary alone. This paper presents a custom, fully self-collected and self-annotated dataset of 1506 apple images (1054 training, 301 validation, 151 test) captured under controlled, fixed-camera conditions and annotated for three target classes: fruit body, stem cavity, and calyx. A YOLO11s detector trained with default hyperparameters is adopted as the baseline, and a systematic, one-factor-at-a-time ablation study is conducted across input resolution, data augmentation policy, optimizer configuration, and lightweight architectural enhancement to identify the factors that most improve detection of these fine-grained landmarks under high inter-cultivar color and texture variability. Neither increased input resolution, nor any of six tested augmentation variants, nor manual optimizer tuning improved on the untuned baseline (F1 = 0.9047); only a same-slot architectural substitution of the backbone's C2PSA block with Coordinate Attention (CA) matched the baseline's overall F1 (0.9038) while reducing parameter count by 10.2% and achieving the study's best mAP@0.5 (0.935) and best stem-cavity F1 (0.8217). A confidence-threshold sweep identified 0.15 as the deployment operating point for this model, and a confirmatory experiment combining the CA-swap architecture with the best-performing augmentation variant showed the two effects do not combine additively, reversing the architectural gain rather than compounding it. The resulting design recommendations --- the CA-swap architecture alone, at a 0.15 confidence threshold --- target real-time apple landmark detection for orientation-aware industrial sorting and alignment systems.

papers.title: Mimicking the zero-field Josephson diode effect with remanent magnetization and self-field
papers.abstract: A Josephson junction whose critical current is larger in one direction than in the other is a diode. With a magnetized barrier, a junction can be a diode at zero applied field, and this is commonly attributed to an intrinsic Josephson diode effect, in which the magnetic barrier breaks time-reversal symmetry. Here we show that the same signatures arise from two ordinary ingredients: the magnetic field of the bias current in the electrodes and the remanent magnetization of the barrier. In cross-type Nb/Pd$_{89}$Ni$_{11}$/Nb junctions, the self-field displaces the interference patterns of the two current polarities in opposite directions. An in-plane remanent magnetization translates the pattern and brings the resulting asymmetry to zero field, where the junction mimics a nonvolatile diode with an asymmetry of 10 to 12% and a polarity set by the magnetization direction. Reversing the current or the field cannot distinguish this mimic from an intrinsic effect, but the wiring can: moving the current lead to the other arm of the electrode across the field reverses the self-field diode, in applied field and at zero field alike, whereas an intrinsic diode would be unchanged. This gives a simple dc test for Josephson diodes in the current-perpendicular-to-plane geometry.

papers.title: Generic singularity formation in two-dimensional Keller-Segel systems
papers.abstract: On bounded domains, the mass-conserving parabolic-elliptic Keller-Segel system admits smooth equilibria at every mass. Nevertheless, we prove that on a disk, an open dense set of positive initial densities leads to finite-time blow-up or infinite-time grow-up whenever the effective mass is at least the critical value $4\pi$. This threshold is sharp: below $4\pi$, every solution exists globally, remains uniformly bounded, and converges to a smooth equilibrium. At the critical mass, all solutions are global, while infinite-time grow-up accompanied by boundary concentration is generic. We extend the result to other bounded planar domains and closed surfaces, obtaining sharp mass thresholds for the round sphere and the flat square torus.

authors.name: Geuntaek Seo
authors.institution: Pohang University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Half-inverse problems for perturbed Bessel operators with a known left-hand potential
papers.abstract: For the regular Sturm-Liouville operator $-\frac{{\rm d}^2}{{\rm d}x^2}+q$ acting in $L^2(0,1)$, the Hochstadt-Lieberman theorem states that one full spectrum together with the potential on either the left half-interval $q|_{(0,1/2)}$ or the right half-interval $q|_{(1/2,1)}$ uniquely determines the full potential $q$. The inverse-square singular term $\tfrac{l(l+1)}{x^2}$ in the perturbed Bessel operator $-\frac{{\rm d}^2}{{\rm d}x^2}+\frac{l(l+1)}{x^2}+q$, acting in $L^2(0,1)$, breaks the left-right symmetry. It is known that, when the right half of the potential $q|_{(1/2,1)}$ is given, the uniqueness of the potential can be established even if a finite number of eigenvalues (depending on $l$) are omitted. In this paper we study the opposite setting--where the left half potential $q|_{(0,1/2)}$ is known--and show that one full spectrum together with finitely many norming constants uniquely determine the full potential $q$. Moreover, we specify the minimum number of norming constants required for the uniqueness. Finally, for positive integer $l$, $L^2$ potentials, and the Dirichlet boundary condition at $x = 1$, we establish the local bi-Lipschitz stability and the local solvability from the full spectrum and finitely many norming constants, assuming the potential on the left half-interval is fixed.

authors.name: Xin-Jian Xu
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Chuan-Fu Yang
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Local Modifications of Nearest-Neighbor and Min-Plus Representations
papers.abstract:
We study how changing a Boolean-valued function at $d$ inputs affects the size and precision of its exact representations. Starting from a representation of size $m$, we prove four bounds, two for nearest-neighbor (NN) representations and two for integer min-plus representations.
  (i) For NN representations on a finite subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $n\ge2$, at most $m+2d$ anchors suffice. The coefficient $2$ is optimal: on a three-point domain, changing one value can increase the minimum number of anchors from one to three.
  (ii) For NN representations on the Boolean cube with rational anchors, let $R$ be the maximum original coordinate bit length, and let $\Delta$ be the maximum bit length of the least common denominator of any one original anchor's coordinates. We construct a representation with at most $m+3d$ anchors on a common dyadic grid and coordinate bit length $O(R+\Delta+\log(n+1))$.
  (iii) For integer min-plus representations on the Boolean cube, we give a construction that keeps the original $m$ forms and their labels and adds at most $d$ new forms. Its maximum weight is at most $W+2n$, where $W$ is the largest absolute original coefficient, including constant terms.
  (iv) For integer min-plus representations on a finite rational domain $X\subset\mathbb{Q}^n$, at most $m+2d$ forms suffice. Their maximum weight is polynomially bounded in $m,d,W,n,|X|$, the coordinate bound, and the common denominator of $X$. The coefficient $2$ is again optimal: on a three-point domain, changing one value can increase the minimum number of forms from one to three.
  These bounds imply stability under polynomially many changes on the cube for polynomial-size representations, including those with polynomially bounded NN coordinate bit length or min-plus weight.

authors.name: Liliia Redina
authors.institution: National Research University Higher School of Economics

papers.title: C-embeddings of spaces of signed measures
papers.abstract: For a Tychonoff space $X$ let $M_a(X)\supset M_\sigma(X)\supset M_\tau(X)\supset M_R(X)$ be the spaces of finitely additive, $\sigma$-additive (Baire), $\tau$-additive and Radon signed measures on $X$, and let $M_\beta(X)$ and $M_d(X)$ be the spaces of compactly supported and discrete measures; all of them are regarded as subspaces of $M(\beta X)=C(\beta X)^*$ with the weak$^*$ topology. We study when $M_p(X)$ is $C$-embedded ($C^*$-embedded) in $M_q(X)$. We prove that $C$-embeddedness, $C^*$-embeddedness and $G_\delta$-density of $M_p(X)$ in $M_q(X)$ are equivalent, and that they are equivalent to a lifting property: for every continuous map $f$ of $X$ into a metrizable compact space, the image of every probability measure in $M_q(X)$ is the image of a probability measure in $M_p(X)$. The main tool is a general theorem, proved in a separate paper, asserting that $C$-embeddedness, $C^*$-embeddedness and $G_\delta$-density are equivalent for dense subspaces of locally convex spaces in the weak topology, and, more generally, of products of first-countable spaces. We characterize the spaces $X$ for which $M_\sigma(X)$, $M_\beta(X)$, $M_d(X)$ and $M_R(X)$ are $C$-embedded in $M_a(X)$ (pseudocompactness, pseudo-$\omega$-boundedness, scatteredness of $\beta X$, and a lifting property of Radon measures, respectively). We give an example of a pseudocompact locally compact space $X$ for which $M_\tau(X)$ is not $C^*$-embedded in $M_\sigma(X)$, and we show that $M_\tau(X)$ is $C$-embedded in $M(\beta X)$ for every $G_\delta$-dense subspace $X$ of a product of metrizable compact spaces. Using a set of universal measure zero, we construct a pseudocompact space $X$ for which $M_R(X)$ is $C$-embedded in $M(\beta X)$, although the restriction to $X$ of a coordinate projection onto $[0,1]$ maps no $\sigma$-compact subset of $X$ onto $[0,1]$.

papers.title: C*-embeddings of spaces of probability measures, nonnegative measures and unit balls
papers.abstract: For a Tychonoff space $X$ and $p\in\{d,\beta,R,\tau,\sigma,a\}$ let $M_p(X)$ be the space of discrete, compactly supported, Radon, $\tau$-additive, $\sigma$-additive or finitely additive signed measures on $X$, regarded as a subspace of $M(\beta X)=C(\beta X)^*$ with the weak$^*$ topology, and let $M^+_p(X)$, $U_p(X)$ and $P_p(X)$ be its subsets of nonnegative measures, measures of norm at most one, and probability measures. In the companion paper it was shown that $M_p(X)$ is $C$-embedded in $M_q(X)$ iff it is $C^*$-embedded iff it is $G_\delta$-dense. We show that $G_\delta$-density of $Q_p(X)$ in $Q_q(X)$ is the same condition for all $Q\in\{M,M^+,U,P\}$, and that $C^*$-embedding of $Q_p(X)$ in $Q_q(X)$ implies $G_\delta$-density, while the converse fails for $Q\in\{M^+,U,P\}$. We prove that $M^+_p(X)$ is $C^*$-embedded in $M^+(\beta X)$ iff $P_p(X)$ is $C^*$-embedded in $P(\beta X)$, that pseudocompactness of $P_p(X)$ implies pseudocompactness of all its powers, and that the unit ball $U_R(X)$ is $C^*$-embedded in $U(\beta X)$ iff $P_R(X)$ is pseudocompact. If $\beta X$ is $\kappa$-metrizable (e.g., a product of metrizable compact spaces or a compact group), then pseudocompactness of $P_p(X)$ and the $C^*$-embeddings of $P_p(X)$, $U_p(X)$ and $M^+_p(X)$ in $P(\beta X)$, $U(\beta X)$ and $M^+(\beta X)$ are equivalent to the $C$-embedding of $M_p(X)$ in $M(\beta X)$. Consequently, $P_\tau(X)$ is pseudocompact for every pseudocompact dense subspace $X$ of a Tychonoff cube. This gives a space $X$ for which $P_\tau(X)$ is pseudocompact while the space $P_R(X)$ of Radon probability measures is not, and answers a question of the first author.

papers.title: Federated Learning for Cross-Regional Epidemic Forecasting with Asynchronous Outbreaks
papers.abstract:
Objective: Epidemic outbreaks are often asynchronous across regions, yet collaborative forecasting is hampered by privacy laws and heterogeneous public health interventions. We developed and evaluated, as a proof of concept, a federated learning (FL) framework for cross-regional COVID-19 forecasting under asynchronous outbreaks among Guangdong, Macau, and Portugal, while maintaining data sovereignty.
  Methods: Using daily case data from WHO and China CDC for the three regions, whose outbreaks were asynchronous and interventions heterogeneous, we trained Long Short-Term Memory networks via FL for short-term forecasting, benchmarked against localized and centralized training using Root Mean Square Error, Mean Absolute Error, and Symmetric Mean Absolute Percentage Error. All experiments used the Flower FL framework with consistent hyperparameters across sites. Publicly available, aggregated case-count data were used so that the centralized benchmark could be computed as a reference.
  Results: The dataset comprised 1,233 daily observations (411 days) of new confirmed COVID-19 cases from November 24, 2021, to January 8, 2023. The earlier Omicron wave in Portugal supplied transmission dynamics that improved forecasts in the later-onset regions of Macau and Guangdong. The FL model achieved a normalized Root Mean Square Error of 0.028, an 88.3% improvement over the local model (0.240) and comparable to the centralized model, with network overhead mainly determined by model size and aggregation rounds.
  Conclusion: FL achieved short-term forecasting accuracy close to centralized training while maintaining data residency, with acceptable overhead. Leveraging asynchronous outbreaks across regions may offer a practical path to privacy-preserving collaborative forecasting, though prospective validation is required.

authors.institution: Macau University of Science and Technology
