Training-time scaffolds, such as strategies or hints added to the prompt during training, offer a natural way to turn this information into guidance, but their design and adaptation are largely left to humans and tailored to specific domains. We introduce AutoScaffold, a unified AI-for-AI framework that turns a student's training experience into adaptive scaffolds, with minimal domain-specific information and no human intervention during training. A frozen teacher periodically examines this experience, diagnoses bottlenecks, and designs scaffolds in two forms: (i) strategies shared across a class of tasks and (ii) hints for individual hard tasks, adjusting the content and amount of support as the student learns. The scaffolds are removed at evaluation. We apply the same framework to ALFWorld, search-based QA, mathematical reasoning, and GPU kernel generation. When evaluated without scaffolds, students trained with AutoScaffold outperform those trained with the corresponding RL baselines in all four domains, with gains of 7.2 points in ALFWorld success and 4.0 points in average QA exact match. On GPU kernel generation, AutoScaffold increases the fraction of tasks with a correct kernel that runs faster than the PyTorch reference by up to 5.0 points. On math, our student surpasses QuestA's reported accuracy using approximately one-third as many student training steps. Analyses show that the teacher identifies a different failure in each task class and shifts its scaffolds from step-by-step workflows to targeted fixes as the student improves, and that its revised scaffolds help the student learn more than keeping the previous scaffold or using no scaffold.

authors.name: Sihan Zeng
authors.institution: Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory

papers.title: Constraining electron heat flux from reduced measurements
papers.abstract: Coronal heating estimates depend partly on electron heat transport. Different electron velocity distributions can match the same observations yet carry different heat fluxes. We ask which measurements are enough to determine heat flux without finding how electrons are distributed across all speeds and directions. The solar wind carries electrons outward from the corona and allows their velocities to be measured directly. Using one Wind measurement, we keep density, mean flow, temperature and angular summaries for each energy channel. In the fixed-bin model, electron distributions that match these quantities have heat fluxes from 3.58 to 19.85 $\mu$W m$^{-2}$. Keeping the correlation between electron motion along and across the magnetic field fixes the heat flux at 11.73 $\mu$W m$^{-2}$, matching the original bin calculation. This recovers heat flux without reconstructing the full shape of the electron velocity distribution. When the measured counts vary, retaining the required correlations leaves the same heat-flux range as direct calculation from those counts. We propose testing coronal observations in the same way to find which features of electron motion they constrain well enough to determine heat transport. Those constraints could help establish the heating requirements used to assess coronal heating mechanisms.

papers.title: Human and Machine Annotations Predict Brain Responses to Naturalistic Movies Across Development
papers.abstract: Naturalistic movie watching provides a powerful framework for studying dynamic brain function, but linking movie content to neural responses typically relies on labor-intensive human annotation. We investigated whether multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can provide scalable socio-affective and semantic annotations for naturalistic fMRI. We compared MLLM-generated theory-of-mind (ToM) and valence ratings with human ratings and with regional BOLD responses across three animated movies. For two of these movies, we combined machine-derived visual features, natural-language scene descriptions, and socio-affective ratings in an ROI-wise encoding model of fMRI data from 66 participants aged 5--22 years. MLLM ratings partially tracked human judgments, but their neural correspondence differed by construct and model: ToM showed the most consistent human--machine overlap in visual cortex, whereas valence correspondence was largely movie dependent. In the encoding model, visual features yielded the strongest and most widespread prediction, whereas scene descriptions were more spatially selective, concentrated in dorsal-attention and visual regions and extending into right lateral temporal cortex. Age-group comparisons suggested feature-specific developmental differences: scene-description encoding in dorsal-attention cortex was higher in the oldest group, whereas visual-feature encoding in salience/ventral-attention, limbic, and control networks peaked in the middle group. Together, these findings indicate that MLLM-generated annotations capture meaningful aspects of human judgments and neural responses, supporting MLLMs as a scalable complement to, rather than a replacement for, human annotation in naturalistic neuroimaging.

papers.title: A Topological Approach to the Discrete Dual Minkowski Problem
papers.abstract: The discrete dual Minkowski problem asks for the necessary and sufficient conditions on a finite discrete measure $\mu$ on $S^{n-1}$ such that $\mu$ is given by the $q^{th}$ dual curvature measure of a convex polytope in $\mathbb{R}^n$. In this paper, using topological degree theory, a novel framework is developed to prove existence of solutions. This approach is applied to the case of polytopes in $\mathbb{R}^n$ for $q>0$ and $n\geq 2$ whose outer normals are in general position while also subject to a constraint on their distribution on $S^{n-1}$. Moreover, existence of solutions is also proved in the plane under a different constraint on the outer normals by proving that a family of non-linear second-order recurrence relations do not have non-constant $N$-periodic solutions.

papers.title: Judicious $r$-partitions of $r$-uniform hypergraphs
papers.abstract: Bollob\'as and Thomason conjectured that every $r$-uniform hypergraph with $m$ edges admits an $r$-partition such that each class meets at least $rm/(2r-1)$ edges. In this paper, we establish a lower bound of $(11-\sqrt{13})m/18$ for every $r\ge 2$. This improves Haslegrave's bound $rm/(3r-4)$ for every $r\ge 8$.

authors.name: Qinghou Zeng
authors.institution: Center for Discrete Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science

papers.title: SPMW: A Grid-Based Programming Model for Scalable Accelerator Design
papers.abstract: Modern accelerators specialize recurring computation and replicate it across regular hardware structures to achieve high performance. Sustaining this parallelism requires equally deliberate data delivery. Yet design tools often express these structures as sequential programs or flatten them into separate hardware modules and connections. This obscures shared patterns and leads to repeated compiler work. We introduce Single Program, Multiple Connected Work Units (SPMW), a grid-based programming model for scalable accelerator design that makes grid regularity a first-class abstraction. SPMW decouples local work-unit behavior from grid connectivity and data delivery. To our knowledge, SPMW is the first programming model to retain regularity throughout the compilation process, combining behavioral HLS with structural RTL generation for both fixed-function and domain-specific instruction-programmable accelerators. We implement SPMW with a Python frontend and an MLIR-based compiler that synthesizes each distinct kernel configuration once for reuse across independent hardware instances. Preserving regularity also enables parallel compilation and functional simulation to accelerate iterative design feedback. We use SPMW to generate a 32x32 systolic array that reduces GEMM latency and parallel kernel-to-RTL compilation time by 4.36x and 619x relative to AutoSA. Our FFT achieves up to 2.65x lower latency than HP-FFT. Our mini-TPU and our SPMW implementation of the FEATHER accelerator demonstrate complex composition and outperform their RTL baselines. Parallel functional simulation provides up to 18.4x speedup over Vitis HLS C simulation on the mini-TPU workloads. SPMW is also agent-friendly: given the same design specification, all five coding agents produce SPMW designs that satisfy the correctness and latency requirements, with 7.51x lower token usage than for SystemVerilog.

authors.name: Niansong Zhang
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Cryohydrologic Flow and Pingo Formation Within Freezing Impact Melts in Occator Crater, Ceres
papers.abstract: Ceres is a volatile-rich dwarf planet in the asteroid belt and a potential relict ocean world. It exhibits surface features indicative of subsurface brine activity, particularly within Occator Crater. High-resolution imagery from NASA's Dawn Mission reveals landslides, gullies, carbonate faculae, and mound-like features resembling terrestrial pingos on the floor of Occator Crater. Some of these landforms have been hypothesized to form from water, either from the ascent of deep crustal brines or from the freezeout of impact melt. Here, we test the hypothesis that pingo-like features can be formed via the freezing of shallow impact melts. We simulate the heat transfer and groundwater flow dynamics of a freezing impact melt deposit on the floor of Occator Crater. We test a comprehensive parameter space of regolith physical and material properties relevant to the cerean environment. We find that impact melt freezinf produces pressure gradients sufficient to drive hydrologic flow within the melt matrix and could transport fluids to the near surface through hydraulic fracturing. For most of the parameter space tested, water volumes delivered to pingo candidates on the surface meet or exceed those likely required for pingo formation. Analogous hydrologic processes may be important in the shallow subsurface of other regions of Occator Crater and Ceres at large as well as other ice-rich planetary bodies.

papers.title: AI is ready, but are the students. From answer-making to sense-making
papers.abstract: Students in introductory physics often struggle with interpreting kinematics graphs, especially when connecting graphical features to physical meaning. We investigated AI tool use in kinematic graphing analysis as an intervention to support active sensemaking. This study examines GPT-5 performance on the Test of Understanding Graphs in Kinematics (TUG-K) and the way students interacted with GPT-5 during introductory physics activities involving graphical analysis. For the first part of the study, GPT-5 responses were evaluated across repeated TUG-K trials and compared to previously reported GPT-4 performance. Following that analysis, student-GPT-5 dialogue episodes were collected and analyzed using an inductive coding scheme. GPT-5 performance results show markedly improved accuracy. Student-GPT-5 dialogue episodes evolved from mostly procedural answer-making requests early in the term, to more reflective sensemaking interactions at the end of the term, suggesting that instructional framing is needed for AI tools to function as meaningful peer-like learning supports.

papers.title: Repertoires of Contention: Building computational tools and infrastructures for community resistance to bitcoin mining
papers.abstract: Recent work in human-computer interaction and allied fields has sought to engage community members as co-designers, facilitators, and decision makers to challenge structural power barriers and knowledge gaps. In this paper, we apply a diverse set of computational techniques to engage and address community concerns surrounding the socio-environmental impacts of the Greenidge Bitcoin mining power plant facility in upstate New York. Through collaborative interactions with community groups, addressing problems ranging from regulatory inertia to thermal water pollution, we aim to facilitate not just the production of new and critical environmental knowledge but also new computationally-supported repertoires of contention: means of contesting the unequal relations of knowledge and power that structure and often determine the outcomes of environmental controversies. We argue such engagements can help support more politically engaged forms of HCI, oriented towards efforts to redress and repair disparities in wealth, knowledge, and influence through strategic sociotechnical interventions and alliances.

papers.title: How anion composition governs structural frameworks and Li-ion transport in oxychloride solid-state electrolytes
papers.abstract: Mixed-anion lithium oxychlorides exhibit high Li conductivity, but the relationship between oxygen content, structural framework, and Li-ion transport remains unclear. Here, crystal structure prediction and molecular dynamics simulations with machine-learning interatomic potentials are used to examine $\mathrm{Li}_yM\mathrm{O}_x\mathrm{Cl}_{6-2x}$ ($M$ = Nb and Ta [Group 5] and $M$ = Ti, Zr, and Hf [Group 4]). Increasing oxygen content changes isolated chloride-rich polyhedra into one-dimensional chains and subsequently more highly connected two- and three-dimensional frameworks. In the Group 5 series, fast Li diffusion occurs over $x \approx 0.67$--1.5, where the Li sites form a three-dimensional percolating network. Potential of mean force maps and nudged elastic band calculations reveal that fast Li-ion transport requires a low-dimensional framework supporting long-range migration through undercoordinated Li sites with low barriers, together with similar energies across Li sites. Finally, we perform fine-grid compositional search, which identifies $\mathrm{LiNbO}_{0.67}\mathrm{Cl}_{4.67}$, $\mathrm{LiTaO}_{0.75}\mathrm{Cl}_{4.5}$, $\mathrm{LiNbO}_{1.5}\mathrm{Cl}_3$, and $\mathrm{LiTaO}_{1.5}\mathrm{Cl}_3$ as stable candidates with predicted room-temperature self-diffusivities of up to $\sim 10^{-6}\,\mathrm{cm}^2/\mathrm{s}$. These findings establish how oxygen content controls framework and Li-ion transport, guiding the design of lithium oxyhalide electrolytes.

papers.title: Stochastic homogenization of $p$-resistance forms on nested fractals
papers.abstract: We study the stochastic homogenization of $p$-energies on infinite nested fractals. We assign i.i.d. random $p$-resistance forms $D_{0,\alpha}$ to level-$0$ cells of an infinite pre-nested fractal, and study the scaling limit of the resulting random $p$-resistance form $\mathcal{D}^{(0)}$. Under a moment condition on the reciprocal of $D_{0,\alpha}$, we prove that the sequence of rescaled and renormalized random energies is almost surely Mosco convergent to an equally weighted self-similar $p$-resistance form. As an application, when $p=2$, we prove the almost sure weak convergence of the associated rescaled continuous-time random walk. In particular, we allow arbitrarily small random conductances and impose no condition on the upper bound of random conductances.

papers.title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
papers.abstract: LLM agents are increasingly used for open-ended, data-driven scientific discovery, yet most of them evaluate hypotheses pointwise, testing an empirical claim $h$ only against its complement $\neg h$. When evidence rejects $h$, the agent learns that one explanation is unlikely but not which alternative the evidence supports. To recover that alternative, we introduce Contrastive Discovery, which replaces the single hypothesis with a contrast set, a scientific question paired with mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive competing explanations. Each experiment is scored by how its evidence redistributes belief across the set, and the question is resolved when belief concentrates on one explanation. Because contrast sets change only the unit an agent proposes and scores, an existing agent can use them to re-evaluate evidence it has already collected or to guide its search. Across six domains, $89\%$ of the pointwise candidates with the largest belief shifts are rejections. On the same evidence, contrast sets resolve $73\%$ of these candidates to a specific alternative. When contrast sets guide search, the agent resolves $67\%$ more questions than pointwise surprisal under the same experiment budget. In a blinded study, $38$ human experts chose the same explanation on $78\%$ of resolved questions and on $82\%$ of questions where the pointwise agent rejected its hypothesis and stopped. Together, these results support explicit competing explanations as a way for discovery agents to resolve more scientific questions from the same evidence and validation budget.

papers.title: The Gene Is Not the Gate: Conceptualizing the Semantic Genome of Quantum Software
papers.abstract:
Quantum software spans applications, program representations, compilers, runtimes, and hardware-facing control. Existing abstractions describe these artifacts and layers, but they do not capture the semantic responsibilities that must remain valid as a computation is transformed across the stack. This limits systematic reasoning about cross-layer correctness, evolution, and reuse.
  We present QGenome, a semantic foundation for quantum software genomics. We define a quantum software gene as a typed, reusable responsibility characterized by an explicit contract, execution context, concrete expressions, and supporting evidence. QGenome organizes genes across five software strata and ten responsibility families grouped into computational semantics, coordination, realization, and assurance. Typed genes compose into pathways and genomes through dependency, refinement, provenance, and phenotype relations, enabling responsibilities to be traced across alternative implementations and execution contexts.
  We illustrate the taxonomy using representative public artifacts across the quantum software stack and define principles for contextual validity, genome evolution, environmental adaptation, and capability expression. Rather than presenting a complete taxonomy or an automated extraction technique, QGenome establishes a falsifiable framework and a concrete research agenda for gene mining, lineage recovery, cross-layer regression testing and repair, and evidence-grounded quantum software agents.

authors.name: Ziming Zhao
authors.institution: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

papers.title: Towards Accessible, Autonomous Photosynthesis Monitoring on Living Leaves
papers.abstract: Photosynthesis is a direct biomarker of plant health and functioning. However, measuring net photosynthesis on individual leaves requires expensive (USD 42,000 - USD 89,000) instruments and manual effort. This limits access to photosynthesis sensing and makes long-term monitoring across multiple leaves difficult. We present a 1000x low-cost, autonomous sensing system that enables longitudinal monitoring of photosynthesis on living leaves over multiple days. Guided by a formative user study with 13 plant biology researchers, the system integrates an automated, leaf-attached chamber with a low-cost CO2 sensor. Built using a 3D-printed clamp and thermoformed dome, the chamber periodically closes to measure CO2 drawdown and reopens to refresh the air. Each chamber costs about USD 62 and operates independently, allowing multiple leaves to be monitored simultaneously without pumps or gas tubing. We characterize each chamber and validate its measurements against a research-grade gas exchange instrument (CIRAS-4) across 29 sessions (R^2 = 0.90). We also demonstrate monitoring of C3 and CAM photosynthesis plants, adaptability to different leaf geometries, and a light-response experiment. In a nine-day deployment, six chambers captured simultaneous CO2 exchange from individual leaves of the same plant during drought and rewatering. Each leaf showed different patterns of nighttime CO2 uptake and recovery, which a whole-plant CO2 measurement instrument would obscure. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of such leaf-level photosynthesis dynamics using independent, low-cost autonomous chambers. Our work opens new opportunities for plant science, education, and data-driven agriculture.

authors.name: Julia Wang
authors.institution: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

papers.title: Weighted-AoI-Driven UAV Trajectory and Reporting for Dynamic CKM Tracking
papers.abstract: Existing channel knowledge map (CKM) construction assumes quasi-static environments, failing when channels rapidly decorrelate. This paper investigates continuous online dynamic CKM tracking over an airborne 2D plane via a UAV fleet. We formulate a long-term error minimization problem under UAV mobility and reporting constraints. This problem, however, is intractable with unobservable errors for unmeasured cells. To tackle this, we propose a metric-driven scheduling approach featuring the Weighted-Age of Information (W-AoI). W-AoI evaluates cells by combining exact temporal staleness with spatial uncertainty predicted by a 2D U-Net. We prove that top-$K$ W-AoI selection maximizes the one-slot error reduction bound. Guided by this guarantee, we develop a lightweight greedy trajectory policy incorporating continuous along-path sensing. Simulations demonstrate our method reduces steady-state error by 3.8 dB$^2$ and 4.8 dB$^2$ over AoI-only and FIFO baselines, closely approaching an idealized oracle.

authors.name: Zeyu Zhao
authors.institution: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

papers.title: EngineAgent: Agentizing On-Device LLM Inference Engines with Inference Stack Hierarchy Awareness and Hardware Abilities
papers.abstract: Rapidly evolving LLM architectures and heterogeneous mobile hardware make supporting new models in on-device inference engines a recurring and costly system challenge. Each model may require coordinated changes across conversion, graph construction, operators, and hardware backends. Existing coding agents often miss these cross-layer dependencies and struggle to diagnose failures across host--device execution paths. We present EngineAgent, an agentic system for automating on-device LLM model enablement. Its key insight is to separate reusable engine and hardware knowledge from model-specific implementation. Before enablement, EngineAgent constructs a hierarchy-aware engine index that captures engine abstraction layers and cross-layer dependencies, and pre-validates backend-specific build, execution, and debugging workflows using already supported models. For each new model, a builder uses this knowledge to coordinate cross-layer changes, while an auditor checks implementation completeness and drives iterative debugging through device-side validation. Across 12 tasks spanning three mobile LLMs and four engine--backend pairs on CPUs, GPUs, and NPUs, EngineAgent achieves 75% end-to-end success with either of two underlying LLMs, versus 33.3% for the strongest coding-agent baseline. Success requires compilation, on-device execution, and output-logit agreement with reference implementations. EngineAgent also reduces average per-task time and model-API cost relative to baselines using the same underlying LLMs.

authors.name: Zhengxiang Huang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Zeyu Zhao
authors.institution: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

authors.name: Chengfei Lv
authors.institution: China University of Mining and Technology

papers.title: SeqFold: Timestamp-Addressable Compressed States for User Action Sequence Backbones
papers.abstract: Existing sequential user modeling methods mainly focus on improving the backbone encoder or learning task-specific user representations for a single prediction objective. We instead study how to export the multi-layer user states of a frozen long-history backbone as compact, timestamp-addressable representations for downstream training backfill and serving. In this setting, the user state at a given timestamp summarizes the user's actions before that time, so downstream systems need only the state aligned to each target timestamp rather than the full hidden-state timeline. To this end, we present \texttt{SeqFold}, a compressed-state interface that combines learned multi-channel fusion, channel-specific temporal decay, and Lookup-Free Quantization (LFQ) to produce compact discrete codes from frozen backbone states. Task-specific decoders then map these shared codes into flexible embedding spaces for downstream models. To make timestamp-addressable export practical at scale, we further develop a fused streaming implementation that updates the fusion recurrence after every action while materializing states only at target timestamps. On large-scale proprietary datasets, SeqFold reduces per-state representation storage by $3{,}400\times$ while preserving most of the downstream ranking performance of the uncompressed model, showing that SeqFold is an effective interface for reusing long-history sequence backbones in downstream models.

authors.name: Duo Zhang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Jian Li
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Veritas: A Verifier Generation Harness for Agent Tasks
papers.abstract: The effectiveness of a self-improving system relies heavily on the quality of its verifier, which judges the outcome of each improvement round. However, the verifiers of most tasks are written by hand, which is expensive and does not scale to tasks that come without one. We propose Veritas, a harness that generates verifiers automatically. Unlike general-purpose agent harnesses, Veritas adds three mechanisms for verifier generation: an evidence header stating what the verifier will observe, a library of domain rules that tasks leave unstated, and authoring principles, partly refined by a self-improvement loop. We evaluate on six benchmarks: four scored by execution, whose official verifiers we first certify, and two that compare pairs of responses. With the model fixed, the verifiers Veritas generates agree better with the official verdicts than those of seven other harnesses on all four execution-scored benchmarks. On the two pairwise benchmarks they are at or near the best. They also agree better than those of the vendor's own harness for two of three other model families. Its mechanisms also improve 9 of 12 harness-benchmark pairs scored by execution across three harnesses.

authors.name: Xingyu Mu
authors.institution: Affiliated Hospital of Guilin Medical College

papers.title: What a CAGE 4 Score Measures: An Audit of a Learned Cyber-Defense Benchmark, Its Reference Defenders, and the Tables Built on Them
papers.abstract: CAGE Challenge 4 is the benchmark on which learned multi-agent cyber defenders are compared. We reproduce its two reference defenders, KEEP and H-MARL Expert, in a pinned container and show that three things read from it measure less than they are taken to measure. First, the simulator silently discards any action asserted for an agent whose previous action is still running, and charges one point for a discarded Restore as for one that runs. The documented observation does not expose the busy flag. Both reference defenders read it in their own wrappers, and switching that check off at evaluation costs KEEP's released policy 99.58 points per episode and H-MARL's 145.98, in both cases the charge for Restores sent to busy agents, with H-MARL's executed actions unchanged step for step. On a supervisory harness, holding interventions until the agent is idle is worth 25.3 and 27.6 points per episode at the published setting. In training, the check decides how a busy step enters the trajectory. Trained without it, KEEP leads at a hundred updates in all four paired seeds and trails from two hundred on in all four. Continued to two thousand updates on three seeds, the repaired recipe ends inside the released interval on one seed and short on two, by 27 and 125 points, a spread across training seeds far wider than the released reproduction interval. Second, the evaluation seeds the environment but not the policy, so a reported mean is one draw, and 88.9% of per-episode outcome variance is the policy's own sampling draw. Third, recovery precision depends on the truth it is scored against. Across five published comparison tables, none states the artifact, sampling, criterion and adversary that would make its numbers comparable. We release the instrument, our patches to both defenders, the traces and checkpoints behind every number, and a five-item disclosure checklist.

papers.title: Sim(3)-TurboReg: Robust and Efficient Scale-Aware Registration via Tri-Scale Consistency
papers.abstract: Feed-forward 3D foundation models recover geometry at high fidelity, yet inference memory constraints keep them from processing long sequences natively. Current streaming systems work around this limit with sliding-window chunking, which introduces severe monocular scale ambiguity. Resolving this ambiguity requires Sim(3) registration that stays accurate and efficient under outlier contamination. We introduce Sim(3)-TurboReg, which reformulates the compatibility graph construction of TurboReg by replacing absolute distance constraints with a strict Tri-Scale Consistency (TSC) criterion. Our analysis shows that TSC suppresses both mismatching and coordinate-distortion outliers. We integrate the resulting solver into existing streaming systems and obtain high-fidelity, kilometer-scale reconstruction for feed-forward models. On controlled unknown-scale registration at 90% outliers, ours matches RANSAC accuracy with 92.5% lower median latency. In DA3-Streaming on KITTI, ours improves mean ATE RMSE by 22.2% and reduces mean end-to-end time by 16.6%. Code: https://github.com/ivan-zzj/Sim3-TurboReg

authors.name: Yutong Hu
authors.institution: Southwest University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Non-abelian $p$-adic Hodge theory and stacks
papers.abstract: In the first half of these notes, we survey some aspects of the stack-theoretic perspective on $p$-adic Hodge theory, with an emphasis on the non-abelian aspects. In the second half, we report ongoing joint work on ``quantizing'' non-abelian $p$-adic Hodge theory.

papers.title: Constant query LCCs over the reals
papers.abstract: This note describes a new construction, found by ChatGPT Astra, of constant query Locally Correctable Codes (LCCs) over the real numbers. Prior constructions of constant query LCCs were exclusive to fields of positive characteristic and were conjectured not to exist over the reals. The construction uses low degree polynomial evaluations over an integer grid, together with a novel sampling procedure which outputs, for a given grid point $P$, a random quadratic curve through $P$ which intersects the grid in many other points (the decoding queries). The sampler is `smooth' in the sense that no grid point is queried with high probability. These codes have the additional property that the queried locations (the curve/grid intersections) are all nearby grid points.

papers.title: A Perspective on Topological Charge Density Wave Materials
papers.abstract: Charge density waves are among the earliest known ordered states in quantum materials, yet they have re-emerged at the center of modern discussions of topology, symmetry breaking, and collective dynamics. In several material classes, charge-density-wave order reshapes electronic bands, boundary states, defect structures, and electromagnetic responses in ways that invite a topological interpretation. Real-space imaging has shown that incommensurate order can form networks of phase defects rather than uniform modulations. Boundary-resolved spectroscopy has revealed in-gap modes whose existence and spatial structure track the charge-density-wave order, although such observations remain confined to a single material family. In Weyl materials, density-wave gaps have been linked to axion-like magnetoelectric response, placing the charge-density-wave phase within a dynamical-field description of the effective action. In kagome metals, charge order is intertwined with Berry curvature, unconventional symmetry breaking, and superconductivity. These developments have led to the term "topological charge density wave," but the phrase describes several physically distinct phenomena. We distinguish three meanings: (i) topology of the order parameter and its defects, (ii) topology of the charge-density-wave-reconstructed electronic structure and its boundary modes, and (iii) axion-like electromagnetic response generated by density-wave order. The experimental and theoretical support for these three meanings differs substantially. This Perspective traces the development of these ideas, clarifies the evidence behind each class, identifies unresolved questions and points of debate, and outlines experimental criteria for establishing topology in charge-density-wave states.

papers.title: On the geometry of Gaussian Mean Shift Detection
papers.abstract:
We consider the problem of detecting a shift in the mean of a standard Gaussian random vector, where the direction of the shift belongs to an arbitrary subset $T$ of the Euclidean unit sphere.
  We introduce a correlation functional $\kappa(T)$ and establish a general lower bound on the detection radius in terms of this functional. We identify regularity conditions under which this lower bound is optimal up to an absolute constant. As an application, we recover some well-known results in the literature such as the detection radius for $s$-sparse unit vectors.

papers.title: Quantifying the Sampling Frequency Invariance of Time-Series Foundation Models for Sensor Data Applications
papers.abstract: Time-Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) are increasingly used in sensor applications, where sampling frequency (SF) varies across sensors, devices, and operating modes (e.g., power saving). Ideally, TSFMs must remain effective during such SF changes, provided the SF retains task-critical bandwidth. In this paper, we stress-test 4 prominent TSFMs: MOMENT, Chronos-2, Moirai-MoE, and TimesFM, to quantify their SF-invariance and investigate whether their behavior tracks the resulting loss of information bandwidth rather than the SF value itself. Our stress-test probes 3 dimensions: (i) the shift in embeddings, (ii) the degradation in forecasting performance, and (iii) the degradation in downstream performance, quantified by three novel metrics: FSI, FDI, and CDI, respectively. To our knowledge, this is the first study to place SF-invariance at the core of TSFM evaluations. Our results characterize: (i) how SF-invariance depends on the margin between signal's native-SF and the bandwidth its task requires, (ii) how much of that invariance the choice of TSFM explains, and (iii) how much of TSFM's performance degradation under a lower SF reflects information loss rather than a limitation of their abilities. These findings reframe SF-invariance as a measurable, signal-aware property of the (signal X TSFM) pair, and guide practitioners on when TSFMs display SF-invariance.

authors.name: Yan-Bo Lin
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: IFRS Compliance Verification: An Open Multi-LLM Benchmark and Content-Conditioned Ensemble Classifier
papers.abstract: Verifying corporate financial disclosures against the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) is a core auditing task in which experts cross-reference disclosures with hundreds of fine-grained regulatory paragraphs: a laborious, costly, and error-prone process that motivates growing interest in large language models (LLMs) as compliance assistants. Yet single-model accuracy remains insufficient for high-stakes use, and naive ensembling is vulnerable to systematic per-model biases that can drag aggregate accuracy below that of the strongest individual annotator. This gap is addressed with a multi-stage framework, supported by a new benchmark of 19,998 IFRS regulation-disclosure pairs comprising 11,161 unanimous multi-LLM labels and 8,837 human annotations on items where the LLMs disagreed. The framework couples a three-stage domain-adapted sentence embedding pipeline (BERT masked language modeling on SEC EDGAR filings, unsupervised TSDAE and SimCSE adaptation, and supervised contrastive alignment) with a learned ensemble classifier that fuses frozen embeddings and LLM probability features from GPT-4.1, Claude Sonnet 4, and Gemini 2.5 Pro via Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) optimized gradient-boosted trees. On the disagreement set, the ensemble achieves 81.7% weighted F1, exceeding the strongest single LLM by 10.4 points and majority voting by 14.6 points, and outperforms eleven unsupervised aggregation baselines; the retrieval pipeline attains Recall@15 of 45.3% on unseen regulations. The dataset, model checkpoints, annotation platform, and classifier implementation will be publicly released.

authors.name: Li Yang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Xinyao Zhou
authors.institution: China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences

authors.name: Chen Shen
authors.institution: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University

papers.title: Nepali-English Code-Mixed Speech Recognition: Data Preparation and Adaptation of a Speech Foundation Model
papers.abstract: Nepali speakers regularly mix English words into conversation, but multilingual speech recognisers often struggle with language switches and the writing script used for English words. We study how to adapt SraVaani, a 449M-parameter hybrid TDT-CTC model, using a 172.8-hour corpus covering six Nepali speech domains. Its pretrained tokenizer does not support digits and several common symbols. Rather than replace it or discard these recordings, we generate Nepali and English readings for numbers and use zero-shot ASR output to select a plausible form. Full fine-tuning reduces test word error rate (WER) from 48.6% to 17.1%; a 12-epoch run reaches 16.3%, compared with 16.4% for fine-tuned Whisper large-v3-turbo. Freezing the encoder increases WER to 25.5%, while excluding numeric clips raises WER on numeric test speech from 14.3% to 21.3%. We also evaluate on FLEURS using both its original references and mixed-script alternatives. The comparison shows that transcription conventions explain part, but not all, of the out-of-domain performance loss.

papers.title: Multifidelity Operator Inference for Non-intrusive Model Reduction under Data Scarcity
papers.abstract: Many-query analyses, in which a computational model is repeatedly evaluated, play an important role in uncertainty quantification and optimization for engineering design. However, many-query analyses can be prohibitively expensive when considering high-fidelity numerical models, especially those governed by partial differential equations (PDEs). Surrogate modeling replaces costly simulations with cheap approximations, enabling practical uncertainty quantification and design workflows. Machine learning (ML) approaches to surrogate modeling have gained significant traction in the development of surrogate models due to their non-intrusive nature; they do not require access to the underlying simulation code. The Operator Inference (OpInf) approach, in particular, fits reduced operators to state and corresponding time derivative data. However, high-fidelity training data is scarce due to limited computational budgets, and OpInf models trained on such scarce data often exhibit high variance, a critical liability in high-risk engineering design. We propose Multifidelity Operator Inference (MF-OpInf), which reduces this variance by supplementing scarce high-fidelity snapshots with abundant low-fidelity data drawn from coarser discretizations of the same problem. MF-OpInf handles data across varying fidelity levels by utilizing a multifidelity linear regression framework to estimate the reduced operators. Numerical experiments on model PDE problems demonstrate that MF-OpInf predicts PDE solution fields with higher accuracy compared to the high-fidelity-only OpInf with the same computational budget.

papers.title: CAFE: Closed-Loop Autonomous Task Formulation and Execution without Instance-Specific Instructions
papers.abstract: Scene-driven robot autonomy requires selecting tasks from observations as well as executing them. We study scene-driven task formulation and execution under predefined cleaning, safety, and storage/organization categories, without instance-specific goals or action sequences. CAFE maintains online memory of objects, functional zones, and execution states. A rule-guided Trigger-LLM admits formulation from accumulated evidence; Draft, Complete, and Audit propose goals, resolve execution details, and check dependencies. Outcomes update memory for correction and subsequent discovery. Evaluation in 12 AI2-THOR scenes compares three backbones and task-complexity tiers using coverage, constraint, and execution metrics. Tri-LLM records higher GCR scores than the evaluated baselines across three backbones and task-complexity tiers. Controls examine completion, auditing, zones, feedback, triggering, and prompt examples. LimoCobot traces illustrate storage, cleanup, and recovery from a failed grasp. The study examines how shared scene state connects task discovery to execution and outcome-driven revision.

authors.name: Mingjia Chen
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Towards Reliable VLM Judges: State-Conditional Invariance and Presentation-Aware Diagnostics
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used as automated judges for multimodal and embodied tasks, yet aggregate accuracy or consistency alone does not reveal whether a judge changes its verdict for the right reason. We propose State-Conditional Invariance (SCI), a reliability principle requiring a judge to remain stable under semantics-preserving changes in presentation while responding to causal interventions that change the task outcome. We instantiate SCI in GridWM-Judge, a simulator-grounded diagnostic benchmark built from deterministic MiniGrid trajectories with aligned Full, evidence-removal, and counterfactual variants, plus presentation and representation probes. Across five diagnostic tasks, GridWM-Judge tests local perception, action-conditioned transitions, presentation stability, representation exchangeability, and Full-CF causal discrimination. Our diagnostic evaluations reveal heterogeneous failure modes, including sensitivity to evidence presentation and encoding, low activation on successful trajectories, and weak paired counterfactual discrimination. Perception-controlled analyses further indicate that visual grounding and objective recovery are substantial, model-dependent bottlenecks. These results motivate jointly reporting correctness, presentation stability, and causal sensitivity instead of relying on a single score.

authors.name: Qinan Zhang
authors.institution: Taiyuan University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Wenjun Lv
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Yu Kang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Jian Di
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Marrying Capacity and Precision for Efficient 2D Gaussian Image Representation
papers.abstract: 2D Gaussian representations provide an explicit and efficient way to represent images, but their rate-distortion performance under limited budgets depends critically on how Gaussian capacity and parameter precision are allocated. Existing methods typically optimize these two resources separately, overlooking content-dependent capacity demands and heterogeneous quantization sensitivity. We present CP-GS, a capacity-precision coupled Gaussian splatting framework for budget-aware 2D Gaussian image representation that jointly optimizes capacity allocation and attribute precision under a shared rate constraint. CP-GS first constructs a content-adaptive Gaussian representation by dynamically reallocating a fixed Gaussian budget from redundant regions to areas with higher representation demand. It then introduces hierarchical distortion-aware representation quantization, using efficient rendering-based calibration to allocate precision across Gaussian attributes and further refine it within heterogeneous attribute groups. Finally, it jointly optimizes Gaussian capacity and attribute precision by constructing candidate representations with different Gaussian counts and precision configurations and selecting operating points according to decoded distortion and actual serialized size. Experiments on DIV2K and Kodak show that CP-GS achieves improved rate-distortion performance over representative 2D Gaussian and implicit neural representations across a range of budgets, while maintaining a fixed overall representation budget and low optimization cost. These results demonstrate the benefit of jointly optimizing spatial capacity and parameter precision for compact Gaussian image representation.

papers.title: Pulse or Provenance? What rPPG-Based Deepfake Detectors Learn
papers.abstract: Remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) has been proposed as a physiological cue for deepfake detection, based on the premise that synthesized faces lack a genuine cardiac signal. We examine what rPPG-style detectors learn on Celeb-DF++ (22 forgery methods) and FaceForensics++ (FF++), using one identically sampled window per real and fake video. On talking-face forgeries, simple chrominance traces reach an AUC of 0.998, exceeding a dedicated rPPG extractor (0.87). Controlled experiments indicate that this signal is not physiological in origin. On fully synthesized forgeries, it is equally discriminative when extracted from background regions or from full frames without face detection, and it is concentrated above the 0.7 to 4 Hz heart-rate band. It is largely removed by shuffling frame order but persists after normalizing resolution, frame rate and encoding, and an independent reimplementation reproduces these findings. Removing high-frequency content makes most synthesized videos appear real, adding it makes real videos appear fake, and injecting a synthetic pulse has little effect. In controlled self-reenactment experiments with two generators, animating a face from a single frame introduces the same high-frequency signal, whereas reconstructing each frame from its own source does not. Face-based chrominance detectors trained on Celeb-DF++ classify over 99% of real FF++ videos as fake, indicating that they largely encode video source rather than manipulation, and a CLIP-based detector exhibits the same behavior. A frozen CLIP backbone matches or exceeds fusions of CLIP with rPPG and frequency features. Finally, we show that the official Celeb-DF and Celeb-DF++ splits share identities and source-video content between training and test, and that custom protocols reusing test videos and identities in training inflate weaker detectors by up to 0.30 AUC.

papers.title: A Margin Perspective on LoRA: Robustness to Catastrophic Forgetting and Adapter Merging (MaLoRA)
papers.abstract: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) is the de facto method for parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large neural networks, achieving strong task adaptation with minimal trainable parameters and low optimization cost. Beyond this efficiency, practitioners have observed two striking properties: \textit{robustness to catastrophic forgetting} and the ability to \textit{merge independently trained adapters} into a single model that performs competitively across multiple tasks. These properties are central to continual and multi-task learning, yet remain poorly understood. In this work, we provide a theoretical explanation through a unified \textit{margin-based perspective}. We analyze LoRA in multiclass linear classification under a near-orthogonal task regime with $\ell_2$-regularization, and characterize the optimal LoRA adapter across regularization regimes. Our analysis shows that, in an intermediate regime of regularization parameters, the optimal adapter aligns with the \emph{max-margin solution} on the fine-tuning data. Building on this characterization, we derive two key consequences. First, we obtain closed-form expressions for the margins on pre-training and fine-tuning data, revealing a precise margin trade-off: the regularization parameter controls the balance between retention and adaptation. Second, we analyze adapter merging, proving that merged models achieve positive margin on each task and deriving optimal mixing coefficients that balance margins across tasks and maximize the margin over their union. These results lead to a simple, training-free merging rule, which we term \textit{margin-based LoRA merging} (MaLoRA). Experiments on modern architectures and real datasets validate our theoretical predictions, showing that MaLoRA matches or outperforms several adapter-merging baselines across a range of vision and language classification tasks.

papers.title: Dependable Long-Horizon LLM Agents: A Trajectory-Centered Empirical Study of Where Errors Enter and Which Controls Reach Them
papers.abstract: When an LLM agent fails part-way through a long task, the usual analysis records a symptom: a failure-mode label, or the agent and step judged responsible. It does not say where the error entered, which state carried it to the symptom, whether anything in the trajectory contradicted it, or which control could have caught it. We define an episode record that ties a candidate fault to its origin, propagation, detection, response and consequence, located by operational phase and state domain, and that names the control families whose observation and reach cover it. We turned the record into a written annotation protocol and applied it to 95 failed runs of six multi-agent systems from the public Who&When and MAD corpora, reading each trajectory in full. Faults enter early (median at 0.18 of the run), mostly as wrong decisions or fabrications over task state, and in 37 of 88 Who&When runs before the step the corpus' human labels mark as decisive. In 72% of failed runs the trajectory already contained evidence against the error before the failure; in 88% of those no agent acted on it. Something flagged a deviation in 31% of runs, but no response removed the deviated state. Independent judges reading the unused evidence, task contracts fixed at admission, and re-checking beliefs against the environment reach most episodes; restoring the agent's own state would have sufficed in 35 of 95 runs. A text scan of the raw corpus also shows that 45% of the hand-crafted Who&When failures ended with a provider content-filter crash after which the harness emitted a final answer no agent produced, a failure class that neither symptom taxonomies nor responsible-agent labels represent. Protocol, records and scripts are included.

papers.title: Attribute-Evidence Learning with Multimodal Prompt for Generalized Category Discovery
papers.abstract: Generalized category discovery (GCD) aims to discover novel categories from unlabeled data by leveraging limited labeled samples from old classes. Existing methods that rely solely on visual cues often neglect the multimodal nature of human perception, prompting recent approaches to incorporate textual information such as category tags and attributes. However, these approaches typically entangle global tags and local attributes within a shared global image representation, rendering attributes unreliable and potentially providing misleading cues that can drive the model toward incorrect predictions. To this end, we propose AptM-GCD, a novel multimodal framework that exploits apt textual guidance through attribute evidence learning and multimodal prompt reasoning. Specifically, we design an Attribute-Evidence Learning (AEL) mechanism that treats attributes as localized visual evidence rather than global category descriptors. By interacting attribute embeddings with patch-level visual tokens, AEL identifies reliable attribute-related regions and extracts discriminative local evidence, thereby reducing the impact of noisy or irrelevant attribute cues. Building upon the extracted evidence, we further develop a Multimodal Prompt Learning (MPL) mechanism to bridge local attribute semantics and global visual understanding. MPL converts fine-grained textual evidence into visual prompts and injects them into a multimodal prompt transformer, enabling attribute information to enhance category discrimination through contextual reasoning without enforcing direct global alignment between modalities. Extensive experiments on six datasets demonstrate that AptM-GCD consistently achieves SoTA performance across both fine-grained and generic benchmarks. Moreover, the proposed framework exhibits strong generalization ability, delivering consistent gains under unimodal and class-imbalanced GCD settings.

papers.title: Partition, Refine, and Detect: Preserving Novel Category Capacity in Open-Vocabulary Object Detection
papers.abstract: Open-vocabulary object detection (OVD) expects the model trained on base classes to recognize both base and novel classes at inference. Typical methods rely on CLIP-style vision-language embeddings, yet the learned space is often biased toward base categories, with limited effective capacity preserved for novel concepts. Such a base-dominated representation can compress novel semantics, leading to semantic collapse and mis-calibrated confidence at inference. To address this issue, we present PR-OVD, a partition-and-refine framework that explicitly reserves capacity for novel categories and strengthens category separation, while being seamlessly integrated into different detector architectures. Specifically, PR-OVD first performs coarse partitioning to build global divisions for base, novel, and an explicit background partition in both visual and textual modalities, preventing object-irrelevant embeddings from leaking into category-specific representations. It then applies category-level refinement within each partition to sharpen decision boundaries and alleviate the lack of fine-grained region-level pretraining in CLIP. To further provide reliable visual anchors for novel categories, we design a cognitively inspired Structure Prompt (SP) that encodes both egocentric attributes and allocentric context, facilitating stable partition-and-refine learning. Extensive experiments on two OVD benchmarks show that PR-OVD delivers an average 6.5\% proportional improvement on novel categories over the state-of-the-art methods. Notably, PR-OVD also benefits other open-vocabulary tasks, including segmentation and classification, further confirming its effectiveness and generality.

authors.name: Yi Liu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Liaoning

papers.title: Extracting Published Discussions of 13,616 Galaxies with Language Models
papers.abstract: Astronomers often have difficulty determining whether an object, such as a star or galaxy of interest, has been discussed in the literature. Existing tools enable object identification and linking in papers but do not record whether an object was genuinely discussed in a paper or just appears in a table or catalog. We address this by using language model agents to identify galaxies discussed in more than two sentences across a corpus of 156,006 arXiv astro-ph papers and extract those discussions. We extract 44,332 discussions of individual galaxies containing 85,314 quotes from 18,641 papers. With sky coordinates for 98.2% of discussions, we group them into 13,616 galaxies. We bring these results together into GalaxyWiki, where users can find literature discussing galaxies, read what was said about them, and follow links to the source papers. The code, dataset, and webpage are available at https://github.com/NolanKoblischke/galaxywiki-paper

papers.title: Near-Optimal Sample Complexity of Deterministic Agnostic PAC Learning
papers.abstract: We study the problem of agnostic PAC learning under deterministic labels, where the examples are labeled by an arbitrary deterministic function, which need not belong to the concept class $C$. This model captures misspecification without stochastic label noise and lies between the realizable and fully agnostic settings. Prior work showed that, when $C$ has finite diameter $K$ and VC dimension $d$, deterministic labels can improve the sample complexity upper bound from the classical agnostic guarantee $O(d/\varepsilon^2)$ to $\widetilde{O}(K/\varepsilon)$, but left a large gap between upper and lower bounds. Our main result sharpens this picture. We prove that every class of VC dimension $d$ and finite diameter $K$ is learnable with sample complexity $\widetilde{O}\left( \frac{K^{1/3} \, d^{2/3}}{\varepsilon} \right)$, and we construct classes for which this bound is tight up to logarithmic factors. We also study the online analogue of this problem and show that the minimax regret is again partly controlled by the diameter of the class. Technically, our upper bounds are obtained via memorization-based learning algorithms that exploit the deterministic label structure.

papers.title: FlowPlan: Reducing the Token Cost of Coding Agents with Abstraction-Guided Planning and Verification
papers.abstract:
LLM-based coding agents such as Claude Code can resolve real-world repository issues, but their iterative interaction loop can be expensive. Existing approaches reduce this cost primarily by limiting, compressing, or selectively avoiding information and actions within the repair process. We investigate a complementary question: Can an agent reason about a repair at an abstract program level, rather than repeatedly operating over raw source code, to reduce both the exploration needed to identify a repair and the repeated checking needed to verify it afterward?
  We present FlowPlan, an abstraction-guided repair approach that structures localization, planning, and verification around per-function control-flow or data-flow graphs. The agent first localizes the candidate fault location on the program abstraction and expresses the intended repair as explicit graph deltas before modifying the concrete source. After the edit, FlowPlan reconstructs the same abstraction and compares the observed structural change with the planned one. Then, a verification checks the complete repair before termination.
  Across all six benchmark-model settings, FlowPlan does not significantly change resolution rate relative to the vanilla agent while reducing token consumption in every setting, significantly in five of six settings. With Claude Haiku 4.5, it uses only 0.46-0.47x the baseline tokens on SWE-bench Pro, 0.32-0.35x on SWE-bench Verified, and 0.68-0.74x on SecBench; with Sonnet 5, it uses 0.72-0.76x, 0.73-0.74x, and 0.92-0.94x, respectively. Overall, FlowPlan achieves the largest token reduction among the compared methods in three of the six settings and ties the strongest compared method in a fourth. Trajectory analysis shows that FlowPlan saves tokens by replacing much of the costly post-edit re-reading and testing with explicit verification and reducing per-call context.

authors.name: Jiho Shin
authors.institution: Korea Research Institute of Chemical Technology

papers.title: A NURBS-enhanced high-order finite-volume method for compressible laminar boundary layers on curved domains with hybrid meshes
papers.abstract: High-fidelity simulation of compressible laminar boundary layers on curved domains requires physical wall boundary treatment and geometric representation compatible with high-order reconstruction, since viscous shear stresses and conductive heat fluxes are concentrated in a thin near-wall region. Conventional high-order methods often suffer from loss of accuracy near curved walls or require complicated wall treatments. To address these issues, in this paper, we develop a NURBS-enhanced $k$-exact finite-volume method for the steady compressible Navier--Stokes equations on hybrid meshes. To incorporate physical wall conditions into the high-order discretization, we develop a wall boundary treatment that employs sequential reconstruction without requiring the reconstruction variables to coincide with those used to prescribe the boundary conditions. The NURBS-based boundary representation is used to obtain a high-order accurate description of curved boundaries, and the diffusive generalized Riemann problem (dGRP) viscous flux is employed to enhance numerical robustness. A variety of numerical examples are provided to demonstrate the high-order accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers.title: Predicting Single-Cell Spatial Gene Expression from H&E using Pathology Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Predicting gene expression directly from hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) images offers a scalable and cost-effective approach to deriving spatial molecular insights from routine histology. Pathology foundation models, typically pretrained using tile-level objectives, may not adequately capture the fine-grained cellular features required for single-cell molecular prediction. In this work, we systematically evaluate and establish domain-informed and task-specific strategies for adapting pathology foundation models to single-cell spatial gene expression prediction. Using paired H&E and Xenium 5K data, our approach improves mean gene-wise Pearson correlation by 2.67x over the standard zero-shot baseline and achieves state-of-the-art performance on this task. We demonstrate strong gene-detection performance across the full gene panel (AUROC = 0.800) and importantly identify that predictive performance varies substantially across biological contexts, with our model achieving its highest Pearson correlation for spatially variable genes (r = 0.643). Our findings demonstrate that, despite the challenges of sparse single-cell measurements, H&E-derived representations can recover biologically meaningful spatial expression patterns, highlighting both the opportunities and limitations of morphology-based molecular inference at cellular resolution.

authors.name: Runmin Wei
authors.institution: The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center

papers.title: Two-component $\gamma$-Ray Structure from the CR Sources
papers.abstract: With the advent of a new generation of observational experiments and the accumulation of data, an increasing number of cosmic-ray sources have been found to exhibit pronounced two-component structures in their gamma-ray spectra above GeV energies. To investigate whether these structures share a common physical origin, we conduct a statistical study of sources exhibiting such features using a two-component model of cosmic-ray sources and examine their gamma-ray emission mechanisms. We find that the ambient environment significantly affects the spectral morphology. Sources located in low-density environments but surrounded by dense molecular clumps exhibit two clearly separated spectral peaks. In contrast, sources embedded in dense environments with additional dense molecular clumps nearby retain two-component spectral features, but the components overlap more smoothly, with the high-energy component appearing primarily as a relatively broad shoulder rather than a distinct peak. Our results lend further support to a physical picture in which high-energy cosmic rays are predominantly supplied by local sources, whereas low-energy cosmic rays arise mainly from the collective contribution of sources in other regions of the Galaxy. We also calculate the neutrino spectra of these sources, providing theoretical predictions for future tests of the model through observations of point-source and diffuse neutrino emission.

papers.title: A new notion of Dirichlet boundary condition for elliptic equation of divergence form
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we consider Dirichlet boundary conditions for elliptic equations in divergence form on rough domains by introducing a truncation-based weak solution framework that circumvents global Sobolev trace obstacles. We establish well-posedness on bounded admissible domains for continuous boundary data and $L^2$
  sources, deriving boundary H\"older regularities that require only uniform ellipticity and an exterior measure-density condition. This approach eliminates the uniform domain regularity and coefficient continuity imnposed in Guam, Wang and Zhou(2026). Furthermore, on sufficiently flat Reifenberg domains, we obtain boundary $C^\alpha $ regularity for any $\alpha\in (0,1) $ using natural energy estimates, thereby bypassing
  $L^p$($p>\frac {n}{2}$) restrictions found in Lian and Zhang(2026). Crucially, we obtain global $H^1$
  regularity for H\"older boundary data ($\alpha>\frac 12$) a posteriori, without requiring small-BMO coefficient assumptions on the coefficients.

papers.title: Forward-Value Discretization: Faster Stochastic Diffusion Sampling Without High-Order Approximation
papers.abstract: Stochastic diffusion samplers often require substantially more neural function evaluations (NFEs) than deterministic samplers to achieve comparable sample quality. Although higher-order discretization accelerates deterministic sampling, its benefits for stochastic sampling remains unclear. We establish matching upper and worst-case lower bounds showing that stochastic samplers with higher-order approximations remain first-order convergent, even with exact score functions. Thus, increasing the approximation order does not generally improve the convergence order. Motivated by this limitation, we introduce forward-value discretization, a training-free framework that evaluates the data/noise prediction model at a lookahead estimate constructed from previous predictions. For deterministic sampling, the resulting Forward DPMSolver (F-DPMSolver), improves sample quality at low NFE budgets through its DDIM-based variant, despite remaining first-order convergent. For stochastic sampling, we develop Forward DDPM (F-DDPM), which evaluates the model at a cleaner lookahead point adjusted for subsequent noise injection. This estimate reuses both the previous model prediction and the previously injected noise. Both variants admit first-order convergence guarantees with one model evaluation per iteration. Across CIFAR-10, ImageNet, FFHQ, and LSUN, F-DDPM consistently achieves lower FID than the evaluated stochastic baselines at matched NFE budgets. With 1.5 times as many NFEs as deterministic baselines, it achieves competitive sample quality, narrowing the practical efficiency gap between stochastic and deterministic sampling. Code is available at https://github.com/Na-Li66/F-DDPM.

authors.name: Yuchen Jiao
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

authors.name: Na Li
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: Nonparametric Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Mixtures of Logistic Regressions
papers.abstract: Mixtures of logistic regressions provide a flexible framework for modeling binary responses, extending standard logistic regression to accommodate unobserved heterogeneity while retaining an interpretable regression structure. In this paper, we study such models with an unspecified mixing distribution. We analyze a sieve nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator (NPMLE) and derive nonasymptotic bounds on the estimation error of the resulting mixture regression function under both fixed and random designs. Our results reveal an explicit tradeoff between statistical estimation error and the approximation error induced by the sieve radius, from which we derive convergence rates under several tail conditions on the mixing distribution. For computation, we propose a finite-particle algorithm that approximates the sieve NPMLE by optimizing the locations and weights of a finitely supported mixing distribution. The method offers numerical advantages over existing algorithms and comes with rigorous convergence guarantees. For any fixed dataset, we establish global convergence of the likelihood to the restricted NPMLE value when the number of particles exceeds a finite threshold. When the true mixing distribution is finitely supported, we further establish uniform global convergence guarantees and derive error bounds that separate algorithmic and statistical errors. Our analysis also yields a denoising bound for the mixing distribution and an identifiability result that complements existing results in the literature.

papers.title: Train on prefill, monitor at decode: Using sparse autoencoders for topic monitoring
papers.abstract: Topic monitoring is the task of labelling the topic of each token in a model's response during generation. Activation-based monitors that run at generation time have so far been trained to detect harmful content and are limited to two or three classes. We introduce TopicScope, a framework for training causal topic classifiers on SAE features that assign a topic to every token, so that the label can change partway through a response. We train three detector architectures on synthetic multi-topic conversations covering seven topics. Across Gemma-3 1B and 4B, monitors trained on features extracted from prefill hidden states were able to generalise to decoding. We also found that the classifiers are robust to perturbations, losing at most 5 macro-F1 points when off-topic asides are inserted, topics are removed or sections are reordered. Ablations conducted to understand the contribution of the SAE revealed that classifiers reaching baseline performance without it were several times larger. Our findings show that compact topic monitors can be trained inexpensively in prefill and deployed during generation. More broadly, our work shows where SAEs are useful beyond safety classification. Our code, dataset and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/Mercity-AI/SAE-Guardrails and https://huggingface.co/collections/Mercity/online-guardrails-using-sparse-autoencoders-6ac602940468c62fefb2b9e8

papers.title: Every hyperbolic knot has an arc-faithful closed braid diagram
papers.abstract: Every hyperbolic knot admits an arc-faithful closed braid diagram, answering Conjecture 29 of McPhail-Snyder. More precisely, any braid representing the knot can be reworded in the same braid group so that the complete holonomy has distinct incoming parabolic fixed points at every crossing. The construction replaces a pinched crossing by five non-pinched crossings when a suitable third strand is adjacent. On $n$ strands it uses at most $2n-1$ letters per replaced crossing. The resulting diagram realizes the complete holonomy by nondegenerate shapes in its four-term octahedral decomposition.

papers.title: Fast Scrambling Cosmology
papers.abstract: Quantum gravity arguments such as trans-Planckian censorship suggest that de Sitter space can only last for a time of order $H^{-1}\ln(M_{\rm Pl}/H)$, corresponding to the fast-scrambling time of black hole and cosmological horizons. We ask whether this clock leaves an imprint on cosmic expansion, via a minimal modification of the Raychaudhuri equation that adds a term $-\Gamma H^2/\ln(M_{\rm Pl}^2/H^2)$ to $\dot H$, with $\Gamma={\cal O}(1)$. The slowly varying $\sigma\equiv\Gamma/\ln(M_{\rm Pl}^2/H^2)\ll 1$ is nearly constant at late times. De Sitter space is replaced by a slowly evolving vacuum (an exact Lambert-$W$ solution), and for constant $\sigma$ the expansion rate is found in closed form for arbitrary matter sources. The correction acts as dark energy with two components: a vacuum mode with $w=-1+2\sigma/3$, and a term that integrates over the history of the cosmic fluids, so that any change in the equation of state of a species leaves a permanent residual; e.g., neutrinos becoming non-relativistic shift the dark energy density by ${\cal O}(\sigma m_\nu^4)$. A covariant clock-field completion reproduces this background, and a term that rescales the gravitational constant governing cosmic expansion removes its short-wavelength instability in the dark-energy era. Big Bang nucleosynthesis constraints give a proxy bound $\Gamma=-3.7\pm6.1$ (68% confidence), while the negative-$\Gamma$ branch qualitatively follows the $w_0w_a$CDM dark energy evolution inferred from DESI DR2 at $z\gtrsim1$. The early-time tracking terms amount to a similar rescaling, for which existing fits to cosmic microwave background (CMB), baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) and supernova data translate into the proxy estimate $\Gamma\simeq-2.8\pm0.9$ ($\sigma\simeq-0.01$ today). These background-level results motivate a dedicated likelihood analysis of structure formation in this theory.

authors.name: Fatima Abbasi
authors.institution: Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research

papers.title: Fast Sampling or High Gain? iP versus PI Control
papers.abstract: Intelligent proportional (iP) controllers, introduced in the framework of model-free control, are often presented as an alternative to proportional-integral (PI) controllers that requires no model of the plant. This paper studies this property for a first-order linear plant under sampled-data implementation with a zero-order hold. When the time derivative of the output is estimated by a backward difference, the discrete-time iP and PI controllers are known to obey the same control law under a one-to-one correspondence between their parameters. Building on this correspondence, the paper derives necessary and sufficient conditions for exponential stability of the iP closed loop, in closed form, in terms of the controller parameters KP and alpha, the sampling period h, and the plant parameters. It then shows that, when the iP parameters are held fixed and the sampling period tends to zero, the closed-loop decay rate tends to the iP gain KP, provided that KP is positive and that the ratio rho between the input gain of the plant and alpha satisfies 0 < rho < 2. One closed-loop pole then behaves as 1 - h KP, while the other tends to 1 - rho. With fixed PI gains, by contrast, the decay rate tends to that of the continuous-time PI loop, which depends on the plant parameters. The two parametrizations therefore suggest different tuning procedures, although they achieve the same closed loops at every fixed sampling period. High gain for the PI is, in some sense, replaced by fast sampling of the iP. The results also make explicit which plant information the iP controller requires: the sign of the input gain and a bound on its magnitude in the limit of fast sampling, and bounds on both plant parameters at a given sampling period. Numerical experiments illustrate these results.

papers.title: RetinexGS: Retinex-Inspired Gaussian Splatting for Low-Light RAW Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Standard 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) pipelines struggle with severely underexposed images, producing unstable colors, floating artifacts, and incomplete reconstructions in dark regions. To better account for noise in these low-light observations, RAW images offer a natural basis for noise-aware reconstruction by preserving linear sensor measurements and providing access to noise metadata. We present RetinexGS, a RAW-domain 3DGS framework that combines Retinex-inspired appearance modeling with sensor-informed optimization for low-light novel-view synthesis. We factorize each Gaussian's color into a view-independent base color and a shared, position- and view-dependent modulation field, regularizing the two components separately to constrain appearance learning from noisy observations. We use DNG noise metadata to weight the reconstruction loss for signal-dependent noise, while distortion-aware rendering avoids spatially resampling RAW targets. To address sparse geometry in dark regions, we introduce depth-guided initialization. We evaluate RetinexGS on three public RawNeRF scenes and two custom-captured low-light RAW scenes. With all methods trained on the same RAW inputs for each scene, RetinexGS outperforms LE3D and RawNeRF in mean sRGB PSNR by 2.18 dB and 2.71 dB respectively, across the five scenes, while supporting real-time novel-view rendering.

papers.title: Residual-Corrected Physics-Informed Neural Network KKL Observers with Input-to-State Stability Guarantees
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural network (PINN) Kazantzis--Kravaris--Luenberger (KKL) observers require an approximate solution to a KKL partial differential equation (PDE) and an approximate inverse of this solution. Either approximation can leave a nonzero estimation bias even without measurement noise. In this paper, we remove both errors from the implemented observer by construction. We build an encoder containing an explicitly invertible neural map. Its closed-form inverse provides the internal state reconstruction used to evaluate the learned KKL residual and correct the latent dynamics. This construction makes the synchronization manifold exactly invariant for every value of the network weights. Based on contraction of the residual-corrected observer dynamics, we prove an input-to-state stability (ISS) result for the implemented error dynamics with respect to measurement noise. A direct consequence is that the estimation error converges exponentially to zero in the noise-free setting. We provide two numerical examples, the Van der Pol oscillator and the chaotic Lorenz system, in which the residual-corrected observers achieve exact noise-free convergence and improved error responses compared with released PINN--KKL baselines.

authors.name: Jun Liu
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: BioMem: Agentic Memory for Biomedical LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated considerable potential in biomedical applications, while agentic memory systems have emerged as a promising approach to preserving and utilizing information across tasks and interactions. However, a fundamental question remains: how effectively and reliably do these systems retain, retrieve, update, and utilize biomedical information? In this study, we systematically investigate agentic memory in the biomedical domain, focusing on task effectiveness, retrieval quality, information fidelity, and long-term robustness. We evaluate five memory approaches across four LLMs in three representative settings: biomedical knowledge reasoning, clinical prediction, and long-term conversational memory. Our analyses reveal how memory construction, evidence relevance, and conversational history shape downstream biomedical performance, highlighting the distinct challenges of retrieving relevant information, preserving its fidelity, and effectively utilizing it for reasoning. Building on these findings, we introduce Hybrid Memory Retrieval and Utilization (HMRU), a training-free framework that jointly enhances evidence accessibility and task-aware utilization to improve biomedical reasoning and long-term conversational memory. HMRU achieves an average relative improvement of 8.6% across biomedical question-answering and conversational memory benchmarks, with additional gains in selected clinical prediction tasks. It further reduces conversational answer errors by 24.9% and closes 48.0% of the performance gap to full-context inference. Our findings provide a systematic characterization of biomedical agentic memory and practical insights into developing more effective and reliable memory-augmented LLM systems.

papers.title: LEASH: Stay Safe in Agentic Robotics
