papers.title: Thermal-pulse-resolved Binary Population Synthesis with Detailed Stellar Models: Implications for Long-period WD+MS Formation
papers.abstract: The origin of the long-orbital-period white dwarf--main-sequence (WD+MS) binaries revealed by Gaia challenges the traditional association of common-envelope evolution (CEE) with short orbital periods. We develop a thermal-pulse-resolved binary population synthesis framework based on 51 detailed MESA evolutionary tracks with initial masses of 1--6 $M_{\odot}$. Applying these tracks to $5\times10^6$ initially sampled binaries, we follow the time-dependent stellar radius, wind mass loss, angular momentum, and tidal interactions, while calculating the envelope binding energy directly from the donor structure at the onset of Roche-lobe overflow. We find that thermal pulses can trigger binary interaction through envelope expansion and tidal orbital shrinkage, while the weakly bound envelopes of highly evolved thermally pulsing asymptotic giant branch (TP-AGB) donors allow CE ejection with limited orbital contraction. For our standard model, with $\alpha_{\mathrm{CE}}$ = 0.3 and $\alpha_{\mathrm{th}}$ = 0.5, systems with orbital periods above 30 days constitute approximately 11.5\% of the resulting TP-AGB-initiated post-CE binaries (PCEBs). Long-period PCEBs can form across a large range of CE parameters and can reach periods of several hundred days even without any internal-energy contribution when $\alpha_{\mathrm{CE}}$ = 1. Their WD masses peak near 0.6 $M_\odot$, whereas systems containing more massive WDs are rare. Moreover, long-period PCEBs closely follow the single-star initial--final mass relation, providing a potential diagnostic of their formation channel in clusters, where progenitor masses can be independently constrained. Our results identify late TP-AGB CEE as a viable contributor to the observed long-period WD+MS population.

papers.title: Global existence and blow-up for a fractional wave equation with logarithmic nonlinearity and strong damping
papers.abstract: This paper studies a fractional strongly damped wave equation with logarithmic nonlinearity. Based on local well-posedness of weak solutions via the Galerkin approximation, we employ the potential well theory to derive the existence of global solutions under subcritical and critical initial energy conditions. Moreover, infinite time blow-up phenomena are obtained under subcritical, critical, and arbitrarily high supercritical initial energy conditions.

authors.name: Jiang Zhou
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: The Proof of the Alon--Kim Conjecture
papers.abstract: In 1997, Alon and Kim proposed an asymptotic edge-coloring bound motivated by a bound on the number of edges in intersecting uniform hypergraphs. The Alon--Kim conjecture asserts that, for fixed integers $k\ge t\ge1$ and $\varepsilon>0$, every $k$-uniform multihypergraph $H$ in which any two distinct edges intersect in at most $t$ vertices satisfies $\chi'(H)\le(t-1+\frac{1}{t}+\varepsilon)\Delta(H)$ whenever $\Delta(H)$ is sufficiently large. In this paper, we prove the Alon--Kim conjecture. Our method combines finite-dimensional convex optimization with probabilistic methods.

papers.title: Plasmons in bilayer graphene with O-type Kekul\'{e} distortion: Electron-hole asymmetry of the effective interlayer tunneling
papers.abstract: The effective interlayer tunneling (EIT) is a key quantity in determining the out-of-phase plasmons of a bilayer structure. Using the tight-binding model and the random phase approximation, we investigate plasmons in bilayer graphene with O-type Kekul\'{e} distortion. Both O/O and G/O bilayers exhibit strong electron-hole asymmetry in the EIT. For the O/O bilayer, the gap of the out-of-phase plasmon remains almost constant as the electron concentration varies, whereas it increases rapidly with increasing hole concentration; hole doping can also lead to stronger anomalous dispersion than electron doping. For the G/O bilayer, enhancing the Kekul\'{e} distortion $\Delta_0$ can weaken the EIT, as reflected by the reduced interlayer hybridization caused by the lifted layer degeneracy, especially for the electron-doped case. For the electron-doped G/O bilayer, the EIT is almost turned off when $\Delta_0=0.3$ from the perspective of the dispersion. Our results imply that switching the doping type between electron and hole can tune the performance of out-of-phase plasmon-based devices by modulating the EIT.

authors.name: Mingyu Wang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Guodong Yu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Quasisymmetric rigidity of self-similar square carpets
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be a self-similar square carpet obtained by subdividing the unit square into $n^2$ congruent cells, deleting a nonempty collection of strictly interior open cells with pairwise disjoint closures, and repeating the same pattern with the same orientation in every retained cell. We prove that every quasisymmetric self-homeomorphism of $S$, equipped with the Euclidean metric, is a Euclidean isometry. The result holds for every integer $n\ge3$ and imposes no symmetry condition on the deletion pattern. Consequently, the quasisymmetric and isometric groups coincide with the stabilizer of the first-generation holes in the symmetry group of the square. The proof combines round uniformization and Schottky-map stabilization with a propagation argument across retained cells. This produces global homothety relations for conjugates of cell contractions and forces preservation of the outer peripheral square. Periodic points on its sides then yield preservation of the corners, reducing the conclusion to the four-corner rigidity theorem for square carpets.

authors.name: Fan Wen
authors.institution: Xi’an University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Recursive memory for prediction and generation
papers.abstract: Recurrent and state-space language models compress the past into a state of fixed size. The state must answer questions about the future now, and it must remain useful as new tokens arrive, including tokens the model samples itself. We show that the second requirement can cost far more memory than the first. For a known hidden Markov source with positive transition probabilities, a state of $O(\log(1/\varepsilon))$ bits answers every question about the future to accuracy $\varepsilon$, however far ahead it looks, because the Bayesian filter forgets its rounding errors. Generating the future is different. When a model feeds each sampled token back into its state, the small errors in its next-token distributions add up, and $T$ tokens can require a state of order $\log(T/\varepsilon)$ bits. The lower bound comes from the KL chain rule: at every step, a model with $K$ states pays for approximating the true next-token distribution by one of only $K$ distributions. The argument applies to any source, including a language model continuing a prompt, and a small-ball estimate makes it tight for two-state sources. The extra $\log T$ disappears if the model keeps private randomness, or if error is budgeted per token, as in perplexity. Statistics of the recent past show the same gap between describing and maintaining. The number of ones among the last $n$ bits takes $\log n$ bits to write down. But if each bit is a noisy copy of the one $n$ steps earlier, tracking that count to a mean-square error $E^2$ well below its variance costs order $n/(1+E^2)+\log n$ bits. Information about each bit must be kept until the bit leaves the window, and a queue holding the counts of recent blocks keeps just enough of it.

papers.title: AnchorMTS: Multi-View Signal Representation and Forecast-Anchored Fusion for Long-Term Time-Series Forecasting
papers.abstract: Long-term time-series forecasters typically optimize a single numerical representation, even though the same history exposes complementary geometry, recurrence, and semantic structure. We propose AnchorMTS, which derives self-aligned visual and textual views from each observed window and uses them only to refine a complete numerical forecast. A trainable evidence path produces a candidate forecast, while a parameter-free output projection enforces an exact per-variable bound on its displacement from the numerical anchor. Across six benchmarks and four horizons, AnchorMTS achieves the best macro MSE/MAE (0.336/0.367) among seven supervised baselines and wins 18 of 24 MSE settings against the cellwise baseline envelope; removing the auxiliary path raises macro MSE to 0.340. The projection leaves 95.8% of candidate refinements unchanged while yielding zero bound violations, showing that complementary multi-view evidence can improve forecasting while its final influence remains explicitly controlled.

authors.name: Tingting Xu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Jiabin Jin
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Oncogene and Related Genes

papers.title: $\mathsf{SVP}_\infty$ Is NP-Hard for Power-of-two Cyclotomic Ideals
papers.abstract:
We prove that exact decision-$\mathsf{SVP}$ in the coefficient $\ell_\infty$-norm is $\mathsf{NP}$-complete for principal ideals and free modules of rank two over the cyclotomic rings $R_n=\mathbb{Z}[X]/(X^n+1)$, where $n$ ranges over powers of two. For each case, we give a deterministic polynomial-time many-one reduction from the Subset Sum problem. For an instance with $s$ positive input integers, the output lattice has dimension $O(s)$. A solution to the original Subset Sum instance can be recovered in polynomial time from any nonzero output lattice vector of norm at most the specified bound.
  We also transfer these reductions from $R_n$ to the power-of-two cyclic rings $S_{2n}=\mathbb{Z}[X]/(X^{2n}-1)$. This gives $\mathsf{NP}$-completeness of decision-$\mathsf{SVP}$ in the coefficient $\ell_\infty$-norm for principal ideals and free modules of any fixed positive rank over these rings.

authors.name: Yansong Feng
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Modelling velocity gradient invariants in turbulence with Lundgren spiral vortex ensemble
papers.abstract: We investigate the joint probability density function $P(Q,R)$ of invariants $Q$ and $R$ of the velocity gradient tensor in the synthetic turbulent field formed from the Lundgren spiral vortex ensemble, which is referred to as the woven Lundgren turbulence (WLT). The WLT inherently captures non-Gaussian vorticity correlations and multiscale interactions, which are essential for reproducing $P(Q,R)$ observed in homogeneous isotropic turbulence. By analyzing the contributions of stretching, winding and dissipation processes in WLT, we demonstrate that the $Q$-$R$ diagram can be divided into three distinct physical regions: a head region dominated by stretching, a body region dominated by spiral vortex arms, and a tail region dominated by dissipation. We systematically vary three key parameters in WLT, the background strain rate, the cutoff age of spiral vortices and the viscous decay factor, and monitor the evolution of $P(Q,R)$ in different topological regions. It is revealed that increasing the stretching rate broadens the head region, larger cutoff ages enhance the inclination of the body region, and reducing viscous factors extends the tail region, thereby mimicking the effects of strain self-amplification and vortex stretching across scales. Based on WLT statistics, we establish and validate an explicit model of $P(Q,R)$ consisting of the stretching, spiral and dissipation contributions. Thus, the WLT provides a physically interpretable framework for understanding the relation between local geometry and global statistics of turbulence.

authors.name: Yue Yang
authors.institution: Beijing Institute of Nanoenergy and Nanosystems

papers.title: Stationary integral cycles asymptotic to a pair of transverse oriented $n$-planes at infinity
papers.abstract: Let $P, Q$ be two oriented transverse $n$-planes in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, $n\geq 2$, which satisfy the equality in the Lawlor--Nance angle criterion. We prove that any stationary integral $n$-cycle in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ with $[P]+[Q]$ being the tangent cone at infinity, in both the current and varifold senses, is a translation of $[P]+[Q]$ or of a Lawlor neck.

authors.name: Zhihan Wang
authors.institution: Institute of Agricultural Resources and Regional Planning

papers.title: A New Computational Model for the Spin-Free Sum-of-Squares Energy Bounds of Electronic Hamiltonian
papers.abstract: Optimizing spin-free sum-of-squares (SOS) energy bounds for electronic Hamiltonians leads to semidefinite programs whose expanded size grows rapidly with the orbital dimension. We derive an exact reformulation of an established spin-free SOS model as a convex quadratic problem over a single symmetric matrix constrained between zero and the identity. Explicit recovery maps connect feasible quadratic-program iterates to certificates in the original SOS formulation, and identify the Frank--Wolfe gap with the separation between recovered primal and dual objectives. We implement the quadratic action through GPU-accelerated Coulomb contractions and solve the reformulated problem using a cached implementation of fully corrective Frank--Wolfe, referred to here as the dimension-reduced simplicial method (DRSM) that caches operator products and optimizes convex-combination weights in a small corrective quadratic program. Numerical experiments cover 65 FCIDUMP models, molecular geometries, and regular hydrogen rings, including original-coordinate recovery checks on nine instances and comparisons with FISTA and a boundary-point SDP solver. On eight H100 GPUs, a cold-start calculation for C$_{720}$ with 10,080 spatial orbitals reaches a freshly recomputed Frank--Wolfe gap of $8.82\times10^{-9}$ hartree in 5.02 hours. Full-space hydrogen-ring calculations reach 10,000 orbitals, with cyclic reduction providing further computational savings. These results show how exact reformulation, data structure exploitation and reuse of Coulomb actions make optimization of the selected large-scale SOS relaxation practical.

papers.title: Particle-hole asymmetry and a fluctuating pair-density-wave state in a lightly doped Mott insulator on the square lattice
papers.abstract: Whether a lightly doped Mott insulator on the square lattice supports robust $d$-wave superconductivity remains a central question in strongly correlated physics and in the microscopic theory of cuprate superconductivity. Experiments and numerical studies reveal a pronounced particle-hole asymmetry, pointing to a delicate competition among $d$-wave superconductivity, pair-density wave (PDW), stripe, charge-density wave (CDW), and antiferromagnetic correlations. Here we combine large-scale DMRG and finite-size PEPS to study the square-lattice $t$-$J$ model at low doping, $\delta \leq 0.1$, while tuning the next-nearest-neighbor hopping $t'$ from the electron-like ($t'>0$) to the hole-like ($t'<0$) regime. The electron-like side supports robust, nearly uniform $d$-wave pairing, whereas decreasing $t'$ induces a period-two plaquette modulation and ultimately produces, on the hole-like side, a charge-dominated state with a strongly suppressed static pairing amplitude. DMRG calculations on open strips and squares, together with PEPS calculations on open squares up to $16\times16$ sites, support this evolution. On squares with $C_4$-symmetric Hamiltonians, both methods find that the pair correlations of the hole-like state select the plaquette momenta $(\pi,0)$ and $(0,\pi)$ and decay within a few lattice spacings, while the dominant charge-density modulation forms a bidirectional checkerboard whose period extrapolates to about $4a_0$, close to that observed in lightly doped Bi-2201. These observations establish a fluctuating plaquette PDW in the lightly doped hole-like regime, in which local pairs carry finite momentum but lack phase coherence. Our results firmly establish particle-hole asymmetry as a central organizing principle for competing pairing tendencies in the lightly doped $t$-$J$ model.

authors.name: Hao-Xin Wang
authors.institution: Yunnan University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

authors.name: Wen-Yuan Liu
authors.institution: Wuhan University of Science and Technology

papers.title: TimeOmni-o1: Bidirectionally Coupling Time Series Foundation Models and LLMs for Multimodal Reasoning and Forecasting
papers.abstract: Time series from real-world systems are often accompanied by text, such as a report on an event that affects them. Two common tasks on these series are understanding, e.g., answering questions about a series, and forecasting its future values. Both tasks require reasoning over the series and the text together. Moreover, understanding outputs text while forecasting outputs a time series, so serving both requires a model that reads and generates both modalities. Large language models (LLMs) read time series as digit tokens and handle long series poorly. Time series foundation models (TSFMs) forecast well from large-scale pretraining but typically neither read nor generate text. Time series language models add a time series modality to the LLM but forecast on the LLM side, leaving the TSFM's pretrained forecasting ability unused. We present TimeOmni-o1, which couples a pretrained TSFM and an LLM bidirectionally. In one direction, the TSFM encodes the series in compressed form for the LLM, which reasons over it together with the text. In the other, the LLM's reasoning is fed back into the TSFM, which produces the forecast conditioned on it. One model architecture thus reads and generates both series and text, reasons in text, and draws on the TSFM's pretrained forecasting ability. To train it, we build MMTR, a multimodal time series reasoning dataset with annotated reasoning traces, covering both tasks across 12 domains with 500k+ samples. On MMTR, TimeOmni-o1 outperforms existing models on both understanding and forecasting across most domains, as well as the LLM and the TSFM inside it when used individually. The gains carry over to three open benchmarks, where it outperforms the dedicated time series models.

authors.name: Wen Wu
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Chao Zhang
authors.institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

papers.title: PyOTIS: an open-source Python package for stream solute transport with transient storage
papers.abstract: OTIS and OTIS-P provide transient-storage transport and parameter estimation, whereas E-OTIS adds coupled water-quality reactions in a separate MATLAB implementation. PyOTIS brings these workflows into an open-source Python package with legacy OTIS input support. Its contribution is software integration: a scriptable interface, structured simulation outputs, Jacobian-based parameter uncertainty, sensitivity analysis, and selectable transport schemes. A browser-based graphical user interface (GUI) provides example loading, custom parameter entry, breakthrough-curve and storage-zone plots, reference overlays, and calibration of supplied cases with confidence intervals. The package retains the OTIS Crank--Nicolson formulation and the E-OTIS reaction network; these are inherited model components rather than new process formulations. Evaluation distinguishes code comparisons, analytical convergence, and fits to observations. For the six OTIS manual examples, the comparisons distinguish model outputs from field observations and include agreement to seven significant figures for the steady-state iron profile. The nine-species E-OTIS comparison reports maximum absolute differences of order $10^{-14}$\,mg\,L$^{-1}$ against MATLAB. The conservative analytical benchmark shows approximately second-order convergence. For Clackamas River calibration, residual sums of squares differ from OTIS-P by 3.65--5.12\%, although individual parameter estimates differ by up to 39.1\%. These results support implementation consistency for the tested cases without establishing unique parameter estimates or validating every reaction pathway. Source code, example inputs, and verification scripts accompany the package.

authors.name: Binbin Wang
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Selective Surgical Action-Center Localization:Retaining Localization Gains through Supervised Scoring
papers.abstract: Surgical action-center localization requires both an accurate reference point and a decision about whether to report it. When frames with and without a reportable center are mixed, the benefit of improved localization depends on which correct candidates survive selection. We present a selective localization pipeline combining heatmap and coordinate supervision with a logistic-regression scorer. The scorer learns to identify predictions with a reportable center and a localization error within a specified tolerance. The internal evaluation uses 5,000 frames from 50 surgical sources, five source-grouped folds and two random seeds. Matched locator and scoring comparisons track correct candidates and their rejection. At an 80% acceptance quota per source and a tolerance of 0.10 times the image diagonal, our method retains 46.08 correct outputs per 100 inputs. The baseline locator with the same scoring approach retains 44.20. The gain is 1.88 (descriptive 95% source-paired bootstrap interval, 0.94 to 2.79). Under entropy-based selection, increased rejection of correct predictions offsets the higher supply of correct predictions on average. For the coordinate-supervised locator, supervised scoring reduces these rejections from 6.15 to 2.99 per 100 inputs. Evaluating retained correct outputs reveals whether a selection rule preserves or erodes an improvement in localization.

authors.name: Guochao Zhang
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Instance-preserving graded semantic reporting for surgical action triplets
papers.abstract: Complete-or-reject reporting of surgical action triplets can discard a correctly identified instrument and action when the target is uncertain. We introduce instance-preserving graded semantic reporting, which separates instance selection from the choice of semantic detail. Each selected instance retains its predicted mask and labels while hierarchical correctness scores guide instrument (I), instrument-verb (IV), or complete instrument-verb-target (IVT) reporting. The utility-increment rule DELTA weighs the expected gain from finer reporting against its error cost. We compare three decision rules on 5,641 test frames from eight surgical videos using fixed predictions and scores. At the 10% development calibration target, DELTA retains correct partial reports for 80.0% of candidates rejected by a matched complete-or-reject baseline (5,329/6,662). Adding IV increases source-normalized weighted correct-report yield by 19.13 to 23.13 per 100 frames across all three rules relative to separately recalibrated I/IVT controls. Weighted reporting risk changes by -0.77 to +1.01 percentage points, with complete correct-triplet counts unchanged or reduced. Graded reporting makes partial surgical predictions available as localized descriptions, with an explicit trade-off between report utility and completeness.

authors.name: Guochao Zhang
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Understanding-First AI Engineering: Purposes, Reference Architecture, and Architectural Patterns for Human Understanding
papers.abstract: AI systems can produce reliable results without developing human understanding. However, human understanding remains valuable for shaping subsequent AI-supported work, forming preferences, governing collective choices and satisfying curiosity, even when human participation is unnecessary for correcting errors. We propose understanding-first AI engineering, which treats purpose-specific human understanding as a first-class design principle guiding requirements, design and operation. The purposes of understanding are organised into four complementary rationales: reflective agency, effective action, collective governance and epistemic value. A reference architecture connects production, verification, use, and learning and exploration through shared records, supporting understanding through explanation and participation. Five candidate architectural patterns guide choices about parallel learning, explanatory models, goal exploration, audience-specific views and distributed expertise. Qualitative scenario analysis of two hypothetical use cases demonstrates how the purpose classification, reference architecture and selected patterns guide investigation, participation and decision processes while retaining operational controls. The cases illustrate design consequences and limitations rather than establish empirical effectiveness. The approach makes human understanding an explicit engineering commitment whose justification need not depend on improving the original AI task.

authors.name: Liming Zhu
authors.institution: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

authors.name: Qinghua Lu
authors.institution: Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation

papers.title: TypedInk: Knowing When Not To Draw
papers.abstract: Can a scientific figure generator know when it does not have enough evidence to draw? Complete-source illustrators map a finished methodology section to a schematic, or a table to plotting code, and are never asked this question because their input is assumed complete. The research record is rarely that complete: an outline, a draft paragraph, a table, or a one-sentence intent, in any combination, and painting measured numbers with an image model when the table is missing is a hallucinated result. TypedInk infers a figure type from {diagram, plot, plate} from a possibly incomplete source and dispatches to the renderer that can honor that type's evidence contract, refusing dispatch when the contract cannot be met. On the six gold plots in TypedFigBench (5 views, n=30), TypedInk's code path inks every gold table token when a table is observed (12/12), refuses the 12 hidden-table views instead of inventing numbers, and marks 6 intent-only views illustrative, with no execution failures. An always-draw coder with no such gate inks 30/30 charts, including all 18 with no table, and recovers zero gold numbers on any of them; two vision-language raters (not humans; human replication is future work) still judge those always-draw charts submittable 17/36 times, against TypedInk's refusal 0/36 times. A diagnostic field ablation of the type router (16 illustrations, 5 views each, n=80) locates where this failure would originate if unchecked: an outline alone yields type accuracy 0.31 and sends every gold plot into an integrity violation, and a chat-model planner narrows but does not close the gap (overall accuracy 0.85, still integrity-failing on 25% of outlines). Diagram-label recall is 0.47 on the full record and 0.19 on an outline. Gold plates are typed at dispatch (oracle integrity-fail 0.00) and rendered as stills.

papers.title: Explicit resonance and bifurcation of symmetric periodic solutions for differential systems with multiple distributed delays
papers.abstract: We investigate the bifurcation of symmetric periodic solutions for differential systems with multiple distributed delays. For general multiple-delay systems with a quadratic potential, we establish a Hamiltonian formulation with a \(P_{n,m}\)-boundary condition and derive explicit Maslov index and nullity formulas. For the special case of two distributed delays, we extend the analysis to general nonlinear potentials. These results yield explicit resonance criteria, bifurcation conditions, and Rabinowitz type and Fadell-Rabinowitz type alternatives for $\mathbb{R} $-distinct solutions.

papers.title: Mean-field BSDEs with jumps under quadratic-exponential growth
papers.abstract: This paper studies the well-posedness of mean-field backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs, for short) with Poisson jumps, where the generator has quadratic growth with respect to $Z$ and exponential growth with respect to $U$, where $(Y,Z,U)$ denotes the solution of this BSDE. First, we prove the existence and the uniqueness of local solutions to mean-field backward stochastic differential equations with jumps (BSDEJs, for short) by using a fixed-point argument. Then, based on these local results, we discuss the solvability of global solutions in the following two cases: in the first one, the generator has linear growth with respect to $Y$ and the corresponding marginal distribution $\mu_1$; and in the second one, the generator has subquadratic growth with respect to the marginal distribution $\mu_2$ and linear growth with respect to the marginal distribution $\mu_3$, corresponding to $Z$ and $U$, respectively. Finally, by employing a Girsanov transformation we establish a comparison theorem for mean-field BSDEJs under quadratic-exponential growth conditions.

authors.name: Juan Li
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Vanishing Theorem of Pin(2)-equivariant Bauer-Furuta Invariants as Stable Sections
papers.abstract: We develop a viewpoint of Pin(2)-equivariant Bauer-Furuta invariant: It can be converted to a section over a finite dimensional Pin(2)-orbit, and it takes values in ordinary stable homotopy class. This viewpoint reveals a topological limitation of the invariant: If the fiber's connectivity exceeds the dimension of the base space, then all sections are homotopic to the trivial section. We use it to recover Lin-Mukherjee vanishing theorem. Furthermore, the family Seiberg-Witten invariant can be obtained from the pullback of such sections to $S^1$-orbit. We use this fact to prove a vanishing theorem of the Pin(2)-equivariant family Bauer-Furuta invariant after two stabilizations.

authors.name: Haochen Qiu
authors.institution: General Research Institute for Nonferrous Metals (China)

papers.title: Taste or Strategy? Nationalistic Bias and Competitor Penalties in Figure Skating Judging
papers.abstract: Many decisions rest on expert panels whose members have ties to some candidates, and favoritism is hard to tell from shared taste or better information. Using a rich dataset from figure skating, we find evidence of a strategic compatriot premium and a targeted penalty on the compatriot's close rivals. The premium falls along a randomly drawn start order and, before 2022/23, rises when close rivals have their own judges on the panel. The penalty grows with the compatriot's placement chances and fades once she is out of contention. A counterfactual analysis shows that these biases can shape close competitions.

papers.title: ABRR: Transforming Temporal Sentence Grounding with Wasserstein-Adaptive Refinement and Precision Ranking
papers.abstract: Temporal Sentence Grounding (TSG) aims to localize temporal segments in untrimmed videos that correspond to natural language queries, a critical task for video understanding with applications in video retrieval, summarization, and human-computer interaction. Despite significant progress driven by transformer-based models, existing TSG methods suffer from two key limitations: quantization errors due to temporal downsampling, which misalign segment boundaries, and suboptimal ranking of predictions based on semantic matching rather than localization precision. To address these challenges, we propose the Adaptive Boundary Refinement and Ranking (ABRR) framework, a novel, model-agnostic post-processing approach that enhances the performance of any TSG model without retraining. ABRR integrates three innovative components: (1) Temporal Distribution Smoothing, which mitigates noise in predicted score distributions using Gaussian kernel convolution; (2) Boundary Refinement via Optimal Transport, which leverages the 2-Wasserstein distance and Sinkhorn iterations to align coarse segment boundaries with true temporal moments, grounded in Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport theory; and (3) Quality-Driven Re-Ranking, which reorders predictions using a composite score balancing localization precision and semantic relevance. By correcting quantization errors and prioritizing accurately localized segments, ABRR achieves substantial improvements over state-of-the-art TSG models. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, including Charades-STA, ActivityNet Captions, and QVHighlights, demonstrate consistent gains at stringent IoU thresholds (e.g., IoU=0.7), alongside enhanced ranking performance. The framework's computational efficiency and compatibility with existing models make it a versatile and impactful solution for real-world TSG applications.

authors.name: Xiang Fang
authors.institution: Wuhan University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Causal mediation analysis for a time-to-event endpoint in the presence of competing events
papers.abstract: Causal mediation analysis is widely used to decompose a treatment's effect into components operating through distinct causal pathways and to characterize the mediator--outcome relationship. In time-to-event settings, competing events --- events that preclude the primary endpoint --- substantially complicate this decomposition. We provide a unified treatment of causal mediation analysis for a time-to-event endpoint under competing events. We show that the total effect on the cause-specific cumulative incidence decomposes into a direct effect, an indirect effect through the mediator of interest, and an indirect effect through the competing events. We develop this decomposition under the natural effects, stochastic interventional effects, and separable effects frameworks, and show that, in certain settings, all three yield identical statistical functionals despite relying on distinct identification assumptions. We derive efficient influence functions for the counterfactual cumulative incidence curves and the decomposed effects, and propose double-machine-learning-type estimators that are multiply robust and attain the semiparametric efficiency bound, with a sensitivity analysis to address unmeasured common causes of time-to-event endpoints. We further study the mediator--outcome response relationship via kernel-smoothed estimands. We apply the methods to immune correlates analyses of COVID-19 vaccine and HIV-1 prevention trials.

authors.name: Yuhao Deng
authors.institution: Ministry of Water Resources of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: Multi-Stage Phase-Aware Self-Supervised Reconstruction for Multi-Echo Gradient-Echo MRI
papers.abstract: Purpose: To develop a phase-aware self-supervised framework for accelerated high-resolution multi-echo gradient-echo (mGRE) MRI that preserves anatomical detail and complex echo information for quantitative mapping. Methods: We developed multi-stage phase-aware self-supervised reconstruction (MSPR-GRE), integrating progressive k-space expansion with phase estimation and refinement. Sequential unrolled networks reconstruct complex multi-echo images and update echo-dependent phase priors. A relaxation-informed temporal subspace is used for acquisitions with at least four echoes, while shorter echo trains are reconstructed in the image domain. Training uses held-out acquired k-space samples without fully sampled targets. Evaluation included 9.4 T ex vivo mouse-brain data 30um eight-echo and 18um dual-echo) and retrospectively undersampled 7 T AHEAD human-brain data, with supervised ablations. Results:MSPR-GRE reduced artifacts in regions of rapid phase variation and preserved fine mouse-brain anatomy. Across five AHEAD test datasets at R = 4, 8, and 12, it generally improved magnitude-image, T2* map, and QSM metrics, particularly at higher acceleration. At R = 12, fourth-echo magnitude NRMSE was 12.09$\pm$0.60% versus 21.55$\pm$1.12% for SSDU. Ablations indicated benefits of phase refinement, while supervised experiments supported multi-stage phase-aware reconstruction. Conclusion: MSPR-GRE improves accelerated mGRE reconstruction and quantitative-map agreement without fully sampled training targets. Further validation of generalizability and phase-estimation accuracy is needed.

papers.title: Positive Codegree Density of Suspensions of Graphs
papers.abstract: We determine the exact positive codegree density of suspensions of graphs $S^r(G)$ when $\chi(G)=t$ and $t-2$ is prime power. The value is $\gamma^+(S^{r}(G)) = \frac{(t-3)(t-2)^{r-1}}{(t-2)^r-1}$. The case of suspensions of $K_4$ gives the positive codegree density of daisies, answering a question of Balogh, Halfpap, Lidick\'y and Palmer. The lower bound construction is from Ellis, Ivan and Leader, while we establish the corresponding upper bound based on a weighted graph inequality.

authors.name: Haiwen Luo
authors.institution: China Iron and Steel Research Institute Group

papers.title: Settling the Burn-in Gap: Sharp Risk Bounds for Tail-Averaged SGD in Linear Regression
papers.abstract: We study the excess risk of constant-stepsize online stochastic gradient descent (SGD) with tail-averaging for high-dimensional linear regression. Building on the instance-dependent spectral framework of Zou et al. (2021), we establish matching initialization-explicit upper and lower bounds on the total excess risk of tail-averaged SGD in terms of the population covariance spectrum $\mathbf{H}$ and initialization $\mathbf{w}_0-\mathbf{w}^*$ whenever a trajectory spectral feedback condition holds. Existing analyses exhibit a fundamental gap in the effective variance: the upper bound of Zou et al. (2021) retains an undamped contribution from the initial error in the head eigenspace $\mathbf{I}_{0:k^\dagger}$, whereas their lower bound omits the variance induced by the head initialization altogether. We show that both the existing upper and lower bounds are loose: the single-hop fast-mode variance contribution from the head initialization is exponentially damped during the burn-in phase, whereas fourth-moment energy scattered from the head initialization into slow spectral modes during the early burn-in steps survives undamped into the averaging window. We prove that our spectral feedback condition is satisfied in two concrete constant-stepsize regimes: (i) for arbitrary covariance spectra $\mathbf{H}$ and any finite horizon, under an explicit horizon-dependent stepsize chosen prior to execution; and (ii) for polynomially decaying spectra $\lambda_i\asymp i^{-a}$ ($a>1$), under a single horizon-independent positive stepsize. Finally, we complement these positive results with explicit one- and two-dimensional separation constructions proving an exponential-versus-polynomial gap in the lower bound of Zou et al. (2021) and showing why fourth-moment assumptions alone cannot determine the asymptotic exponential decay rate without additional structural conditions.

authors.name: Qingyue Zhao
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Boundary-controlled irreversible port--Hamiltonian modeling and structure-preserving discretization of tubular reactors
papers.abstract: This paper presents a boundary-controlled irreversible port-Hamiltonian model and a structure-preserving spatial discretization for a non-isothermal tubular reactor with axial convection, variable-density momentum dynamics, chemical reaction, mass diffusion, heat conduction, and jacket heat transfer. Reaction, diffusion, and heat conduction are described by irreversible port-Hamiltonian channels, whereas convection and momentum are represented by a weighted Eulerian interconnection. The boundary ports recover the axial energy flux and the corresponding entropy flux. A partitioned finite-element method is then formulated in conservative coordinates using a power-preserving change of variables. The semi-discrete model satisfies the Hamiltonian balance and a discrete entropy balance with non-negative entropy production due to reaction, diffusion, heat conduction, and jacket heat transfer. Numerical results for an open tubular reactor are validated against independently computed continuous steady boundary-value solutions and show the transient temperature, composition, and velocity profiles in the very-low-Mach regime. The same discretization is also tested with reciprocal Soret--Dufour coupling, for which the discrete entropy production remains non-negative.

authors.name: Weijun Zhou
authors.institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

papers.title: AdaFCP: Local Neural Functional Representations for Industrial Change Detection
papers.abstract: Industrial sensor measurements often form ordered functional profiles in which persistent operating-regime changes may be confined to short within-cycle regions. Fixed projections can dilute such changes, whereas data-adaptive representation learning complicates reliable statistical testing. This paper proposes adaptive functional change-point detection (AdaFCP) for retrospective detection of a single functional mean change. A compact window and neural basis learn a change-sensitive functional projection by matching the CUSUM path of projected scores to single-change templates. Standardized peak-CUSUM scanning then provides the detection statistic and transition estimate, while the fitted weights identify the contributing within-cycle region. Theoretical analysis characterizes the population path-matching signal and derives an optimal-direction signal-to-noise benchmark. Full-pipeline permutation calibration accounts for adaptive representation learning and restart selection, providing finite-sample false-positive control under exchangeability. A decision-preserving early-stopping variant, AdaFCP-ES, further reduces calibration effort without altering the fixed-budget test decision. Simulations demonstrate advantages over several fixed representations for localized oscillatory changes, while strong analytic and multiscale controls remain competitive. Applications to injection-molding pressure profiles and a nuisance-matched hydraulic benchmark illustrate transition localization and interpretable within-cycle diagnostics, while highlighting the need for dependence-aware calibration in naturally ordered industrial data.

papers.title: Pseudo-marginal Sampling for Selective Inference
papers.abstract: Inference after adaptive selection must account for selection bias. One approach is to condition on the selected event, but for complex selection procedures, the resulting conditional distribution can be analytically intractable and require sampling-based methods. Rejection sampling provides a natural baseline: it repeatedly draws from a proposal and retains only samples that reproduce the observed selection. This can be prohibitively expensive when the selection event is rare. We address this computational bottleneck with a pseudo-marginal Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm that samples from the selective distribution. Using a weak Poincar\'e inequality, we analyze its computational efficiency relative to rejection sampling and identify when it can offer substantial gains. In the classical file-drawer problem, we derive precise computational costs for both methods, illustrating exponential improvement as the selection event becomes increasingly rare. In numerical experiments involving complex selection procedures without tractable conditional distributions, the pseudo-marginal sampler is often hundreds of times more efficient than rejection sampling, while the resulting tests achieve nominal selective Type I error.

papers.title: Impact of Reduced-Order Modelling on Sum-of-Squares Region-of-Attraction Certification for Grid-Forming and Grid-Following Converters
papers.abstract: With the increasing penetration of power-electronic equipment, the transient stability of grid-forming (GFM) and grid-following (GFL) converters is increasingly characterized through the region of attraction (ROA) of the post-fault equilibrium. Sum-of-squares (SOS) programming yields certified inner approximations of the ROA, yet its computational cost grows rapidly with system order. Reduced-order models are therefore widely used to reduce computational cost and, more importantly, to enable analytical investigation. However, ROA analyses based on these models often assume that reproducing the converter's transient response, or retaining more dynamics in the correct time-frame, is sufficient to preserve the ROA of the full-order system. Using time-domain ODE simulations as a reference, the SOS-based ROA of each reduced-order GFM and GFL model is assessed against both its own simulated ROA and that of the corresponding full-order model, thereby separating SOS-induced conservativeness from model-order-induced ROA distortion. The results indicate that increasing reduced-order model complexity does not necessarily improve SOS-based ROA fidelity. In the cases examined, more complex reduced-order models yield lower SOS coverage of the full-order reference ROA, despite closer ODE-boundary agreement in some regions. Model selection should therefore consider both full-order ROA fidelity and certified coverage of the practical operating range, rather than model complexity alone.

papers.title: Failure of endpoint estimates for lacunary bilinear spherical maximal functions on Heisenberg groups
papers.abstract: We prove that the lacunary bilinear Nevo--Thangavelu spherical maximal operator on the Heisenberg group $\mathbb H^n$ does not map $H^1(\mathbb H^n)\times H^1(\mathbb H^n)$ into $L^{1/2,\infty}(\mathbb H^n)$ for any $n\geq1$. We obtain this result by lifting the Euclidean counterexample in our recent result (arXiv:2610.40100) to the Heisenberg group.

authors.name: Ji Li
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: GEMOR-GS: Global Extrinsic-calibration-refined Mapping and Online Relocalization for 3D Gaussian-Splatting SLAM
papers.abstract: Photorealistic and metrically consistent world representations are a primary requirement for LiDAR--inertial--visual SLAM systems that serve robots over continuous operation. 3D Gaussian splatting makes such representations attainable by supplying an explicit, renderable, and queryable scene model. We present GEMOR-GS (Global Extrinsic-calibration-refined Mapping and Online Relocalization for 3D Gaussian-Splatting SLAM) to make the Gaussian map geometrically accurate, globally refined, and re-enterable, providing a better appearance for robot perception and decision-making. To improve the 3DGS map, the LiDAR--camera extrinsic is first estimated offline by direct-method alignment over dedicated calibration segments and reused by all following online and offline processes. Under the calibrated geometry, keyframe poses and Gaussian parameters are refined alternately under a gated differentiable-rendering and LiDAR--projection objective. The final global reconstruction is then rebuilt from the refined keyframe schema with all online constraints lifted. For the robot SLAM lifecycle, the method recovers the pose from the 3DGS map after tracking loss through an XFeat bypass map, RANSAC-PnP coarse localization, and Gaussian RGB-D warp refinement. Experiments on one self-collected and five public sequences quantify each element: the offline reconstruction wins all paired keyframes against the online map by 14.3--19.9 dB, improves PSNR by approximately 9 dB over Gaussian-LIC2, and achieves 86--100% held-out relocalization success tied to extrinsic quality. The results show that GEMOR-GS improves the geometric accuracy, appearance fidelity, and re-enterability of the 3DGS map, serving as a dependable robot world model for SLAM and downstream tasks.

authors.name: Yuchen Yang
authors.institution: Beijing Academy of Agriculture and Forestry Sciences

authors.name: Hesheng Wang
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: Compute the Interactions, Not the Attributes: What a Fact Layer Must Supply in the Chinese Sexagenary System
papers.abstract: Language-model systems in rule-governed domains often pair the model with a deterministic fact layer, but which facts that layer should supply is rarely measured. We measure it in the Chinese sexagenary system underlying BaZi chart analysis, where every fact has one table-checkable value: 682 items over twelve fact categories and 160 transit--natal collision items, posed closed-book, with the reference table, and with computed facts at increasing levels. In eleven open-weight models answering directly, errors concentrate where attributes must be combined: none gets more than 4\% of sexagenary days or 1\% of collisions right. Static attributes have no consistent effect, and the complete relation list leaves most direct-answering models near zero although it contains the answer. A query-filtered layer (exploratory) raises Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-32B to 78--92\% and four further models to 96--100\%. Three proprietary reasoning models compute 68--95\% of collisions unaided. On chess positions, under predictions locked in advance, attributes again do not substitute for relations and listed distractors are misattributed. The fact layer must supply computed interactions; how they are presented depends on the model and the domain.

authors.name: Huixue Han
authors.institution: National Health and Family Planning Commission

papers.title: Optimal Trading Speed on Blockchain
papers.abstract: On blockchain-based exchanges, faster blocks weaken the priority-fee competition among arbitrageurs and shift rents from the block producer to them. Equilibrium liquidity peaks at an interior block speed; beyond a threshold, an active liquidity provider cream-skims and passive capital shrinks. Evidence from the Base Flashblocks upgrade, a tenfold block-speed increase, confirms the predictions. Priority-fee bids decrease sharply and arbitrageurs' net profit rises. The active liquidity provider rebalances faster, avoids toxic flow, and earns a higher profit. Pool depth falls and effective spreads widen despite closer tracking of external prices.

authors.name: Shihao Yu
authors.institution: China Institute of Water Resources and Hydropower Research

papers.title: DrugCoding: A Scientific Programming Agent for Drug Discovery
papers.abstract: Drug discovery involves multiple interconnected research stages, including molecular design, property prediction, and virtual screening. These processes are characterized by complex workflows, interdependent computational tasks, and diverse specialized tools, placing substantial demands on the coordination of scientific models and computational resources. However, existing large language model (LLM)-based scientific agents still face challenges in autonomous planning of complex tasks, adaptive selection of specialized models, and reliable execution of multi-stage scientific computations, limiting their effectiveness in automating complex drug discovery workflows. To address these challenges, we propose DrugCoding, a scientific programming agent system that integrates scientific task planning, adaptive model routing, multi-agent collaboration, and programmatic tool execution. DrugCoding enables autonomous task planning and dynamic model adaptation for complex research objectives. It can flexibly invoke specialized scientific models, autonomously generate and execute code according to task requirements, and leverage multi-agent collaboration to support efficient execution and reliable validation of complex scientific tasks. To evaluate DrugCoding's performance in scientific tool invocation and multi-stage task execution, we conduct multi-turn tool-calling experiments across diverse language models and scientific tool interfaces. Experimental results demonstrate that DrugCoding achieves an average session-level Pass@1 of 97.35% on the full benchmark, outperforming the strongest baseline, Codex, by 9.24%. On the challenging subset, DrugCoding achieves 97.92%, exceeding the strongest baseline.

papers.title: NIF-VIO: Visual--Inertial Odometry Across Inertial and Non-Inertial Reference Frames
papers.abstract: Conventional visual--inertial odometry (VIO) assumes that observations from cameras and an inertial measurement unit (IMU) are jointly consistent in an inertial reference frame. However, this assumption breaks down under non-inertial conditions. Inside accelerating or rotating carriers, visual observations of the interior reflect carrier-relative motion, while IMU measurements contain additional carrier-induced components, which can compromise conventional fusion. We therefore present NIF-VIO for localization relative to the local environment across inertial and non-inertial reference frames. It adapts visual--inertial fusion based on measurement consistency. As inertial conditions change, early constraint isolation is combined with local reoptimization to limit error propagation before inconsistency confirmation and repair the affected local geometry. Under non-inertial conditions, a compact model with temporally shared parameters is introduced to account for carrier motion while preserving inertial information that complements visual constraints. Experiments on public benchmarks and a self-collected dataset demonstrate that NIF-VIO achieves competitive performance under inertial conditions and improved localization accuracy and availability under non-inertial conditions.

papers.title: Overcoming Dynamic Range Limitations in Computational Hyperspectral Imaging
papers.abstract: Computational hyperspectral imaging offers compact spectral sensing, yet imaging high-dynamic-range (HDR) scenes remains challenging. Accurate spectral reconstruction requires encoded measurements to remain within the calibrated linear-response range and above the noise floor. Due to unequal spectral responsivities across the encoding mask, individual channels reach their reliability limits at vastly different incident signal levels. Measurement reliability therefore depends on both exposure time and encoding channel, making it challenging for a single exposure to preserve spectral information in highlights and shadows simultaneously. Here, we demonstrate a physics-guided multi-exposure fusion framework that operates directly in the encoded measurement domain. An analytical reliability prior and learned spatially varying, channel-specific adjustments jointly determine adaptive fusion weights. Measurement-domain spectral-angle supervision further constrains relative channel responses for downstream spectral inversion. The set-wise formulation accommodates varying numbers and configurations of input exposures. We further implement the framework on a 9-channel broadband-encoded stochastic hyperspectral camera, incorporating full-field sensor-response characterization and channel-aware reliability gating. Simulated HDR benchmarks show lower reconstruction errors than representative fusion methods, while controlled spectral measurements and practical HDR scenes confirm improved spectral fidelity and extended usable dynamic range. Measurements using an optical-density target further establish a 16.0-dB increase in spectral reconstruction dynamic range relative to the best fixed single exposure.

authors.name: Zhihai Yao
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: TRUER: Test-Time Reward Correction Using an Error-Aware Rectifier for Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Test-time reinforcement learning enables language models to adapt using rewards derived from their own answers. However, majority voting can reinforce incorrect solutions even when correct alternatives are available. Our training audit shows that false positives (incorrect responses receiving positive rewards) dominate reward errors. We focus on a practical regime where ground-truth rewards are difficult to obtain at scale, while a limited labeled source set is available. We introduce TRUER, a framework that uses limited supervision to train a reward rectifier that distinguishes correctness from consensus. To achieve this goal, we train the rectifier with an emphasis on incorrect majorities and correct minorities, targeting cases where consensus and correctness disagree. After that, we freeze the rectifier and use it to correct rewards during subsequent test-time adaptation. By improving reward accuracy and thereby model performance, TRUER consistently outperforms naive TTRL in both metrics across all evaluated configurations.

papers.title: Scalar-Induced Gravitational Waves Probing Phase Transitions in the Standard Model and Beyond
papers.abstract: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) are unique messengers of physics in the early Universe and possible sources for the observed data from pulsar timing arrays (PTAs). It has been demonstrated that SIGWs have the potential to probe cosmological phase transitions via measurement of the equation of state and sound speed of the cosmic thermal bath, which have non-trivial time dependence during phase transitions. In this work, we improve on existing studies of SIGWs in a time-dependent background with time-dependent initial conditions and an entropy-conserving thermal history of the Standard Model (SM). We provide possible physical explanations for features of the gravitational wave spectrum from phase transitions, the most prominent of which for a scale-invariant curvature spectrum is a step due to entropy dilution. We show that current and future gravitational wave observations across a wide range of frequencies can probe phase transitions in the SM and physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM). Signals from the QCD crossover appear around 10 nHz, inside the observable window of PTAs. We perform data analyses using NANOGrav 15-year data, showing a mild preference for the QCD crossover over standard radiation domination for two choices of curvature spectra. BSM phase transitions in the TeV range lead to signals around mHz, which are accessible in future space-based experiments such as LISA, Taiji and TianQin.

authors.name: Peizhi Du
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Xiang-Xi Zeng
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Organic-Inorganic Composite Materials

papers.title: Local well-posedness, wave breaking and ill-posedness for the unidirectional non-local wave model
papers.abstract: In this paper, we first establish local well-posedness (existence, uniqueness and continuous dependence) for the Cauchy problem associated with the unidirectional non-local wave model in the Besov spaces $B^s_{p,r}$ with $s>1+\frac{1}{p}$ and $1\leq p,r\leq\infty$, as well as in the critical Besov spaces $B^{1+\frac{1}{p}}_{p,1}$ with $1\leq p<\infty$. Next, by exploiting the fine structure of the equation and performing a delicate analysis of the commutator terms, we establish a new sufficient condition for wave breaking without using any conservation law. Finally, we prove that the model is ill-posed in $B^{1+\frac{1}{p}}_{p,r}$ for $1\leq p\leq\infty$ and $1<r\leq\infty$. Our analysis further clarifies the well-posedness theory and wave-breaking behavior of the unidirectional non-local wave model arising from the motion of a cold plasma in a magnetic field, which refines and improves previously known related results.

authors.name: Shaojie Yang
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Time-Varying Photonics: A Review of Theory, Phenomena, and Experimental Platforms
papers.abstract: Time-varying photonics opens new avenues for controlling waves through engineering material properties in time. In this review, we introduce the basic concepts and theoretical tools for describing temporal interfaces, time-periodic systems, and space-time media, as well as review representative experimental approaches across different photonic and wave platforms. We further discuss characteristic phenomena enabled by temporal modulation, including coherent wave control, parametric amplification, nonreciprocity, and topological effects. This review provides a unified pathway for understanding time-varying photonics and outlines its current challenges and future opportunities in both fundamental physics and practical applications.

papers.title: Learning the Brownian Motion in Machine Learning for Parametric Parabolic PDEs: A Backward Quadrature Approach
papers.abstract: We propose a backward quadrature learning (BQL) method for solving high dimensional parametric semilinear parabolic partial differential equations (PDEs). To the best of our knowledge, this work is the first to extend the applicability of BSDE-based stochastic numerical methods to this class of PDEs. Specifically, inspired by the approach of learning the random variables (LRV)~\cite{BeckerJentzenMullerWurstemberger2024}, BQL incorporates learnable quadrature for Brownian increments at each time level into the backward recursion of BSDEs, enabling more efficient layerwise approximation of local conditional expectations. Furthermore, BQL introduces a continuation surrogate to facilitate the transfer of value-function information from subsequent to preceding time levels, avoiding nested quadrature while controlling the propagation of local approximation errors. Our main theoretical contribution is the derivation of a global error bound that explicitly characterizes the decomposition of the total error, together with a proof of first-order mean-square convergence under suitable approximation and integrability assumptions. Finally, numerical experiments demonstrate that BQL achieves competitive solution accuracy while substantially reducing the amortized computational cost per query. For the HJB benchmark across the tested dimensions, with $Q=7$ parameter queries, BQL achieves computational cost reductions of approximately 40-fold and 4-fold compared with P$^2$INN~[2] and FBSNN~[3], respectively.

papers.title: Dual-Core Tensor Wheel Decomposition with Structure-Cached Acceleration for Tensor Recovery
papers.abstract: Tensor wheel decomposition captures complex correlations in high-dimensional data through interactions between outer-ring factors and a high-order central core. However, updating these components requires the explicit construction and manipulation of large-scale matrices, which limits computational efficiency and incurs particularly high computational and memory costs for the central-core update. To address these limitations, we propose dual-core tensor wheel decomposition (DCTW), which factorizes the central core into two lower-order cores linked by a shared latent bond. Each core is coupled to a different group of outer-ring factors. We further propose a structure-cached acceleration strategy that avoids explicit large-scale matrix multi- plications and caches intermediate tensors generated during tensor network contractions for reuse across block updates. This reuse reduces redundant computation and avoids the explicit construction of large matrices. Complexity analysis and experiments show that the strategy based on structural caching accelerates optimization compared with explicit and implicit up- date schemes while limiting the increase in peak memory as the ranks grow. Experiments on color video completion and robust denoising show that DCTW matches or outperforms representative tensor network methods in reconstruction quality, computational efficiency, and scalability.

papers.title: On $q$-Ary $t$-Designs from Codewords of Every Nonzero Weight in Linear Codes and Their Duals
papers.abstract: The paper investigates when the codewords of every nonzero weight in a linear code form a $q$-ary $t$-design and how to generalize the property to its dual code. We reduce the verification of this property to a prescribed range of low weights. Specifically, for MDS codes, we show that the $q$-ary $2$-design property at every nonzero weight is equivalent to that at any fixed nonzero weight. As an application, we prove that the codewords of every nonzero weight in a $[q+1,3,q-1]_q$ MDS code and its dual hold $q$-ary $2$-designs if and only if $q$ is even. We also establish a duality principle. When $t\le\min\{d,d^{\perp}\}$, the codewords of every nonzero weight in a linear code form a $q$-ary $t$-design if and only if the same property holds for its dual code. We then investigate narrow-sense antiprimitive BCH codes $\mathcal{C}_{(q,q+1,\delta,1)}$ and their duals. For $q=2^m$ and $\delta=2^r$ with $1\le r<m$ and $\gcd(r,m)=1$, the codewords of every nonzero weight in these codes form $q$-ary $2$-designs. Furthermore, for $\delta=4$ and $q=2^{m}$ ($m\ge4$), we establish that the minimum-weight codewords of $\mathcal{C}_{(q,q+1,4,1)}$ form a $q$-ary $2$-design if and only if $m$ is odd.

papers.title: Margin-Guided Token Credit for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
papers.abstract: In reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, a language model is rewarded for a correct final answer, and GRPO passes that reward to every token of the solution in equal measure. We instead place the credit where the model hesitated, in a method we call MCPO (Margin-Credit Policy Optimization). We measure hesitation by the top-2 margin $M=p_1-p_2$ of the policy's next-token distribution, map it to a score with two fixed thresholds, and spread each solution's advantage over its tokens so that the mean stays unchanged. The margin is read from a forward pass the trainer already performs, so the method needs no extra model evaluation and no batch statistics. We train MiniCPM5-2B-Base with LoRA for 200 steps on 2,048 DAPO-Math problems and evaluate on six competition-math benchmarks. MCPO beats an unmodified GRPO baseline for all five data seeds, by 6.55 points of macro avg@32 on average (95\% CI $[4.1, 9.0]$), and a Qwen3-4B-Base replication improves for all three seeds ($+4.75$). The gain is largest on problems that GRPO solves only some of the time and grows with $k$ in pass@$k$, reaching 13.8 points at pass@32. MCPO models also write two to three times longer answers, and runs that write longer score higher; our experiments do not separate the two effects.

papers.title: ScaleBrain: A Scale-Consistent Framework for EEG Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Foundation models pre-trained on large unlabeled electroencephalography (EEG) corpora have emerged as a transformative paradigm for Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) applications. Recent EEG foundation models have shown that multi-scale representations derived from fixed-length patches can improve EEG representation learning. Existing frameworks commonly construct temporal scales through feature-level operations. However, these operations leave the correspondence between learned features and scale-specific characteristics of the original EEG signals implicit. Moreover, when the self-supervised objective is not aligned with the multi-scale input representations, information at some temporal scales may receive insufficient supervision during pre-training. In light of this, we propose ScaleBrain, a scale-consistent pre-training framework that explicitly coordinates multi-scale representations of EEG from both the model input and optimization objective sides. Specifically, ScaleBrain introduces multi-scale EEG tokenization to represent the same EEG segment through analysis windows with different temporal spans and shared temporal anchors, and pairs these representations with scale-specific reconstruction to align with the multi-scale input structure and provide supervision across temporal resolutions during self-supervised learning. We further develop an axial spatio-temporal attention mechanism to contextualize the fused multi-scale representation along spatial and temporal dimensions. Extensive evaluations on six public BCI benchmarks against 12 representative baselines show that ScaleBrain achieves the highest mean Balanced Accuracy on five datasets and ranks third on the remaining one, with only 5.0M parameters, demonstrating strong performance and favorable parameter efficiency.

authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China
